chapters.title: Chapter 1 · Two Births Foretold; John Is Born
chapters.intro: The author first explains why he is writing. Then come two announcements: the angel Gabriel tells the old priest Zechariah that his barren wife Elizabeth will bear a son, to be named John, and tells the virgin Mary that she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear Jesus. Mary visits Elizabeth and speaks a song of praise. John is born, and Zechariah, able to speak again, blesses God.

verses.en: Since many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,
just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word handed them down to us,
it seemed good to me also, having followed everything closely from the start, to write it out for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,

cmp.note: 提阿非罗是这卷书题献的人，「大人」是对有地位的人的尊称；他是谁，书里没有说。和合本把这个称呼挪到了第 1 节的开头。
cmp.en: Theophilus is the person the book is addressed to, and “most excellent” is a form of address for someone of rank; the book does not say who he was. The Union Version moves the address to the start of verse 1 as 提阿非罗大人 (Tí’āfēiluó dàrén, “Your Excellency Theophilus”).

verses.en: so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah; and he had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

cmp.note: 犹太祭司分成二十四班，轮流到耶路撒冷的圣殿当值，每班一个星期（见旧约《历代志上》第 24 章）；亚比雅是其中一班的名字。
cmp.en: The Jewish priests were divided into twenty-four divisions that took turns serving at the temple in Jerusalem, a week at a time (1 Chronicles 24); Abijah is the name of one of them.

verses.en: And they were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
And they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.
Now it happened, while he was serving as priest before God in the order of his division,
according to the custom of the priesthood it fell to him by lot to enter the sanctuary of the Lord and burn incense.
And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of incense.
And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense.
And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
for he will be great before the Lord, and he must never drink wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
And he will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

And he will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to children and the disobedient to the understanding of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a people prepared.”

cmp.note: 这句话出自旧约《玛拉基书》4:5–6：上帝说，在主的日子来到以前要先派先知以利亚来，使父亲的心转向儿女。
cmp.en: The phrase comes from Malachi 4:5–6, where God says that before the day of the Lord he will send the prophet Elijah to turn the hearts of fathers to their children.

verses.en: And Zechariah said to the angel, “By what shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in her days.”
And the angel answered and said to him, “I am Gabriel, who stand before God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
And look, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time.”
And the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they wondered at his delay in the sanctuary.
And when he came out he was unable to speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary; and he kept making signs to them and remained mute.
And it happened, when the days of his service were completed, that he went away to his home.
And after these days his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself hidden for five months, saying,
“Thus the Lord has done for me in the days when he looked on me, to take away my disgrace among people.”
Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a town of Galilee named Nazareth,
to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary.
And coming in to her, he said, “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you.”
But she was greatly troubled at the saying, and wondered what sort of greeting this might be.
And the angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
And look, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.
He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.”
And Mary said to the angel, “How will this be, since I do not know a man?”
And the angel answered and said to her, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the holy one to be born will be called Son of God.
And look, Elizabeth your relative has also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren;
for nothing will be impossible with God.”
And Mary said, “Look, the slave of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.
Now Mary arose in those days and went with haste into the hill country, to a town of Judah,
and she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
And it happened, when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, that the baby leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit,
and she cried out with a loud cry and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
And why is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For look, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy.
And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her from the Lord.”
And Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,

cmp.w: Megalynei hē psychē mou ton kyrion
cmp.note: 第 46–55 节是马利亚的颂词，传统上按拉丁文译本的第一个词叫「尊主颂」。它的许多句子取自旧约，尤其是《撒母耳记上》2:1–10 哈拿的祷告。原文是诗的写法，白话照意思写成句子，没有凑成诗。
cmp.en: Verses 46–55 are Mary’s song, traditionally called the Magnificat after its first word in the Latin version. Many of its lines echo the Old Testament, especially Hannah’s prayer in 1 Samuel 2:1–10. The Greek is poetry; the Chinese renders the sense in plain sentences without trying to make verse of it.

verses.en: and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
for he has looked on the humble state of his slave. For look, from now on all generations will call me blessed,
for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
And his mercy is for generations and generations to those who fear him.
He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
He has brought down rulers from thrones and lifted up the humble.
He has filled the hungry with good things, and the rich he has sent away empty.
He has helped Israel his servant, remembering mercy,
just as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his offspring forever.”
And Mary stayed with her about three months and returned to her home.
Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son.
And her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.
And it happened on the eighth day that they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to call him Zechariah after the name of his father.
And his mother answered and said, “No; he shall be called John.”
And they said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.”
And they made signs to his father, asking what he wanted him to be called.
And asking for a writing tablet, he wrote, saying, “John is his name.” And they all wondered.
And at once his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he began to speak, blessing God.
And fear came on all who lived around them, and all these things were talked about throughout the whole hill country of Judea.
And all who heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying, “What then will this child be?” For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him.
And Zechariah his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,
“Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited and brought redemption to his people,
and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,
just as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old,
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,
the oath that he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that we, rescued from the hand of enemies, might serve him without fear
in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.
And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give knowledge of salvation to his people in the forgiveness of their sins,
through the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
to shine on those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 · The Birth of Jesus; the Boy in the Temple
chapters.intro: The Roman emperor orders a registration, and Joseph takes the pregnant Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born and laid in a feeding trough. An angel brings the news to shepherds in the fields, and they hurry to see the baby. Later his parents take him to the temple, where the old man Simeon and the prophetess Anna speak about the child. The chapter ends with Jesus at twelve, staying behind in the temple and questioning the teachers.

verses.en: Now it happened in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole inhabited world should be registered.
This was the first registration, made when Quirinius was governing Syria.
And all went to be registered, each to his own town.
And Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
to be registered with Mary, who was betrothed to him and was pregnant.
And it happened, while they were there, that the days were completed for her to give birth,
and she bore her firstborn son, and wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no place for them in the guest room.

cmp.note: 原文 phatnē 是喂牲口的食槽，不一定是喂马的，和合本译「马槽」。katalyma 可以指客店，也可以指家里招待客人的房间（22:11 同一个词指「客房」）；和合本取「客店」，白话取「客房」。
cmp.en: Greek phatnē is a trough for feeding animals, not necessarily horses; the Union Version has 马槽 (mǎcáo, “horse trough”). Katalyma can mean an inn or the guest room of a house (the same word is “guest room” in 22:11); the Union Version takes it as 客店 (kèdiàn, “inn”), the plain Chinese as “guest room.”

verses.en: And there were shepherds in that same region, living out in the fields and keeping watch by night over their flock.
And an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they feared with a great fear.
And the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid; for look, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people:
for today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord.
And this will be the sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a feeding trough.”
And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among people of his good pleasure.”

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「归给他所喜悦的人」（eudokias）；多数较晚的抄本末尾少一个字母（eudokia），意思变成「平安在地上，善意归给人」。和合本这里的读法和底本一样。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads “among people of his good pleasure” (eudokias); most later manuscripts have the word without its final letter (eudokia), giving “on earth peace, good will toward people.” The Union Version follows the same reading as this edition here.

verses.en: And it happened, when the angels had gone away from them into heaven, that the shepherds were saying to one another, “Let us go over to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
And they came with haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the feeding trough.
And when they had seen it, they made known the saying that had been spoken to them about this child.
And all who heard wondered at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these things, pondering them in her heart.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told them.
And when eight days were completed for circumcising him, his name was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,

cmp.note: 按旧约《利未记》第 12 章，妇女生了男孩以后要过四十天才算洁净，期满要到圣殿献祭。
cmp.en: Under Leviticus 12 a woman who had borne a son was counted clean only after forty days, and then had to bring an offering to the temple.

verses.en: just as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord,”

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《出埃及记》13:2、12：头胎的男孩都归上帝。
cmp.en: The quotation is from Exodus 13:2, 12: every firstborn male belongs to God.

verses.en: and to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

cmp.w: zeugos trygonōn ē dyo nossous peristerōn
cmp.note: 出自《利未记》12:8。那里规定的祭物本来是一只羊羔，买不起羊羔的人可以改献两只斑鸠或两只小鸽子。
cmp.en: From Leviticus 12:8. The offering prescribed there is a lamb; those who cannot afford a lamb may bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons instead.

verses.en: And look, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon, and this man was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
And he came in the Spirit into the temple; and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him according to the custom of the law,
he took him into his arms and blessed God and said,
“Now, Master, you are letting your slave depart in peace, according to your word,

cmp.w: Nyn apolyeis ton doulon sou, despota
cmp.note: 第 29–32 节是西面的颂词，传统上按拉丁文译本开头的两个词叫「西面颂」。这里的「主人」（despotēs）和「奴仆」是一对词，说的是主人放一个当完差的奴仆离开；和合本把「离去」直接译成「去世」。
cmp.en: Verses 29–32 are Simeon’s song, traditionally called the Nunc Dimittis after its opening words in Latin. “Master” (despotēs) and “slave” go together: a master is releasing a slave whose duty is done. The Union Version renders “depart” directly as 去世 (qùshì, “pass away”).

verses.en: for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared before the face of all peoples,
a light for revelation to the nations, and glory for your people Israel.”
And his father and mother were wondering at the things being said about him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, “Look, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that is spoken against,
and a sword will pierce your own soul also, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
And there was a prophetess, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in many days, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
and then as a widow until she was eighty-four. She did not leave the temple, serving night and day with fastings and prayers.

cmp.note: 原文可以读成「守寡直到八十四岁」，也可以读成「守寡八十四年」。白话与和合本的正文取前一种；和合本原书在这里有小字注「或作就寡居了八十四年」。
cmp.en: The Greek can mean “a widow until she was eighty-four” or “a widow for eighty-four years.” Both Chinese versions take the first; the Union Version adds a small-print note giving the second.

verses.en: And coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to God and spoke of him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
And when they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town, Nazareth.
And the child grew and became strong, being filled with wisdom, and the favor of God was upon him.
And his parents went every year to Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover.
And when he was twelve years old, they went up according to the custom of the feast;
and when they had completed the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and his parents did not know it.
Supposing him to be in the company of travelers, they went a day’s journey, and they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances,
and not finding him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him.
And it happened after three days that they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
And all who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
And when they saw him they were astonished, and his mother said to him, “Child, why have you treated us this way? Look, your father and I have been looking for you in great distress.”
And he said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in the things of my Father?”

cmp.note: 字面是「在我父的那些（事或地方）里」，说得很省。可以理解为「在我父的家里」，也可以理解为「办我父的事」。白话取前一种，和合本取后一种（「以我父的事为念」），英文照字面。
cmp.en: Literally “in the things of my Father,” a compressed phrase. It can be taken as “in my Father’s house” or as “about my Father’s business.” The plain Chinese takes the first; the Union Version takes the second with 以我父的事为念 (yǐ wǒ fù de shì wéi niàn, “mind my Father’s affairs”); the English keeps the literal wording.

verses.en: And they did not understand the saying that he spoke to them.
And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. And his mother kept all these things in her heart.
And Jesus advanced in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and people.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 · John the Baptizer; Jesus Baptized; the Family Line
chapters.intro: John is baptizing around the Jordan and calling people to repent; he tells the crowds, the tax collectors and the soldiers what each should do, and says that one stronger than he is coming. Herod shuts John up in prison. After Jesus is baptized and while he is praying, the Holy Spirit comes down on him and a voice from heaven calls him the beloved Son. The chapter ends with the family line of Jesus, counted backward from Joseph to Adam.

verses.en: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,

cmp.w: en etei pentekaidekatōi tēs hēgemonias Tiberiou Kaisaros
cmp.note: 提庇留在公元 14 年继位作罗马皇帝，他在位的第十五年大约是公元 28 到 29 年。这里的希律是第 1 章那位希律王的儿子，只管加利利等地，称号是「分封王」（tetraarchēs）。和合本的「巡抚」，本站写「总督」。
cmp.en: Tiberius became emperor in 14 CE, so his fifteenth year is about 28–29 CE. This Herod is a son of the King Herod of chapter 1 and ruled only Galilee and nearby lands, with the title “tetrarch.” For the governor the Union Version has 巡抚 (xúnfǔ); this site writes 总督 (zǒngdū).

verses.en: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
And he went into all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one calling out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.

cmp.note: 第 4–6 节引的是旧约《以赛亚书》40:3–5。《马可福音》和《马太福音》只引到「修直」为止，这卷书多引了两节，一直引到「所有的人都要看见上帝的救恩」。
cmp.en: Verses 4–6 quote Isaiah 40:3–5. Mark and Matthew stop at “make his paths straight”; this Gospel quotes two more verses, down to “all flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

verses.en: Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be made low, and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough ways smooth;
and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.’”
So he was saying to the crowds that came out to be baptized by him, “Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Bear fruits, then, worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father,’ for I say to you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.
And already the axe is laid at the root of the trees; every tree, then, that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.”
And the crowds were asking him, saying, “What then shall we do?”
And he answered and was saying to them, “Whoever has two tunics, let him share with the one who has none, and whoever has food, let him do likewise.”
And tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what shall we do?”
And he said to them, “Collect nothing more than what has been appointed for you.”
And soldiers also were asking him, saying, “And we, what shall we do?” And he said to them, “Do not extort from anyone or accuse falsely, and be content with your wages.”
Now as the people were in expectation, and all were wondering in their hearts about John, whether he might be the Christ,
John answered, saying to all, “I baptize you with water; but one who is stronger than I is coming, the strap of whose sandals I am not fit to untie; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, to clear his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”
So with many other exhortations he was bringing good news to the people.
But Herod the tetrarch, being rebuked by him about Herodias, his brother’s wife, and about all the evil things that Herod had done,
added this also to them all: he shut John up in prison.
Now it happened, when all the people were baptized, and when Jesus also had been baptized and was praying, that the heaven was opened,
and the Holy Spirit came down on him in bodily form, like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased.”
And Jesus himself, when he began, was about thirty years old, being the son, as was supposed, of Joseph, the son of Heli,

cmp.note: 第 23–38 节是耶稣的家谱。它和《马太福音》第 1 章的家谱方向相反（这里从耶稣往上数，一直数到亚当和上帝），从大卫到约瑟这一段的人名也大多不同；两份家谱为什么不同，经文没有说明。原文每一代只有一个「某某的」，白话照和合本写成「某某是某某的儿子」。
cmp.en: Verses 23–38 give the family line of Jesus. It runs in the opposite direction from the one in Matthew 1 (here upward from Jesus, all the way to Adam and to God), and between David and Joseph most of the names differ; the text does not explain the difference. The Greek has only “of So-and-so” for each generation; the plain Chinese, like the Union Version, spells out “A was the son of B.”

verses.en: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
the son of Joshua, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
the son of Jesse, the son of Jobel, the son of Boaz, the son of Sala, the son of Nahshon,

cmp.note: 这一节有两个名字，底本的写法（Iōbēl、Sala）和多数抄本的（Ōbēd、Salmōn）不同，指的是同样的两个人。白话照和合本写「俄备得」「撒门」，英文照底本拼。
cmp.en: Two names in this verse are spelled differently in this site’s edition (Iōbēl, Sala) than in most manuscripts (Ōbēd, Salmōn); the same two men are meant. The plain Chinese uses the Union Version’s 俄备得 (Ébèidé, “Obed”) and 撒门 (Sāmén, “Salmon”); the English follows the edition’s spelling.

verses.en: the son of Amminadab, the son of Admin, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,

cmp.note: 底本在亚米拿达和希斯仑之间有两代（Admin、Arni）；和合本所据的抄本这里只有一代（亚兰）。各抄本在这一处出入很大。白话照底本，两个名字是本站照音写的。
cmp.en: Between Amminadab and Hezron this site’s edition has two generations (Admin, Arni); the text behind the Union Version has only one, 亚兰 (Yàlán, “Aram”). The manuscripts vary widely here. The plain Chinese follows the edition, with the two names transliterated by this site.

verses.en: the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 · The Testing; Rejected at Nazareth; a Day in Capernaum
chapters.intro: Jesus spends forty days in the wilderness and three times refuses the devil’s tests, then returns to Galilee. In the synagogue of Nazareth, his hometown, he reads a passage from Isaiah and says it is fulfilled today; the townspeople first praise him, then turn furious and try to throw him off a cliff. He goes to Capernaum, drives an unclean demon out of a man in the synagogue, heals Simon’s mother-in-law and many others, and moves on to proclaim in other towns.

verses.en: And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was being led by the Spirit in the wilderness
for forty days, being tested by the devil. And he ate nothing in those days, and when they were completed he was hungry.
And the devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become a loaf of bread.”
And Jesus answered him, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone.’”

cmp.w: Ouk epʼ artōi monōi zēsetai ho anthrōpos
cmp.note: 引的是旧约《申命记》8:3。本站的底本只引到「不是单靠饼」；多数较晚的抄本后面还有「而是靠上帝的每一句话」（《马太福音》4:4 有这半句），和合本跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The quotation is from Deuteronomy 8:3. This site’s edition stops at “not by bread alone”; most later manuscripts add “but by every word of God” (the half-line found in Matthew 4:4), and the Union Version follows them.

verses.en: And leading him up, he showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in a moment of time.
And the devil said to him, “To you I will give all this authority and their glory, for it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
If you, then, will worship before me, it will all be yours.”
And Jesus answered and said to him, “It is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.’”

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《申命记》6:13。三次试探的次序，这卷书和《马太福音》第 4 章不同：那里圣殿在第二、高山在第三，这里反过来。
cmp.en: The quotation is from Deuteronomy 6:13. The order of the three tests differs from Matthew 4: there the temple comes second and the mountain third; here it is the other way round.

verses.en: And he brought him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here;
for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you, to guard you,’

cmp.w: Tois angelois autou enteleitai peri sou
cmp.note: 这一节和下一节引的是旧约《诗篇》91:11–12。
cmp.en: This verse and the next quote Psalm 91:11–12.

verses.en: and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.’”
And Jesus answered and said to him, “It is said, ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
And when the devil had finished every test, he departed from him until an opportune time.
And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and a report about him went out through the whole surrounding region.
And he was teaching in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and as was his custom he went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
And the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him, and unrolling the scroll he found the place where it was written,

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor; he has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to send out the oppressed in release,

cmp.note: 第 18–19 节引的是旧约《以赛亚书》61:1–2，中间「叫受压迫的得自由」一句出自《以赛亚书》58:6。「膏」是把油倒在人头上的仪式，表示这个人被选立担当使命；「基督」这个称号的字面意思就是「受膏的人」。
cmp.en: Verses 18–19 quote Isaiah 61:1–2, with the line “to send out the oppressed in release” taken from Isaiah 58:6. To “anoint” is to pour oil on someone’s head, marking the person as chosen for a task; the title “Christ” literally means “anointed one.”

verses.en: to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”
And rolling up the scroll, he gave it back to the attendant and sat down; and the eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed on him.
And he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.”
And all were bearing witness to him and wondering at the words of grace that came out of his mouth, and they were saying, “Is this not Joseph’s son?”
And he said to them, “Doubtless you will quote to me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself. Whatever we heard was done in Capernaum, do here also in your hometown.’”
And he said, “Truly I say to you that no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
But in truth I say to you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut for three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land,
and Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to Zarephath of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.

cmp.note: 这件事见旧约《列王纪上》第 17 章；下一节乃缦的事见《列王纪下》第 5 章。西顿在以色列北边的海边，乃缦是叙利亚人：两个得到帮助的都不是以色列人。
cmp.en: The story is in 1 Kings 17; that of Naaman in the next verse is in 2 Kings 5. Sidon lies on the coast north of Israel and Naaman was a Syrian: neither of the two who were helped was an Israelite.

verses.en: And there were many with skin disease in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was made clean, but only Naaman the Syrian.”
And all in the synagogue were filled with rage when they heard these things,
and they rose up and drove him out of the town, and brought him to the brow of the hill on which their town was built, so as to throw him down the cliff.
But he, passing through the midst of them, went on his way.
And he went down to Capernaum, a town of Galilee, and was teaching them on the Sabbath;
and they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
And in the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice,
“Ah! What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God.”
And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him.” And the demon, throwing him down in their midst, came out of him without harming him at all.
And amazement came on all, and they were speaking to one another, saying, “What is this word, that with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out?”
And a report about him was going out into every place of the surrounding region.
And rising up from the synagogue, he entered the house of Simon. Now Simon’s mother-in-law was held by a high fever, and they asked him about her.
And standing over her, he rebuked the fever, and it left her; and at once she got up and began to serve them.
Now as the sun was setting, all who had any who were sick with various diseases brought them to him; and laying his hands on each one of them, he healed them.
And demons also were coming out of many, crying out and saying, “You are the Son of God!” And rebuking them, he would not let them speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.
And when it was day, he went out and went to a deserted place; and the crowds were seeking him, and they came to him and tried to keep him from going away from them.
But he said to them, “I must bring the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns also, for I was sent for this.”
And he was proclaiming in the synagogues of Judea.

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「犹太的各会堂」；多数抄本是「加利利的各会堂」，和合本跟的是后一种。这里的「犹太」一般理解为泛指犹太人居住的整片地方（包括加利利），而不是专指南边的犹太地区。
cmp.en: This site’s edition reads “the synagogues of Judea”; most manuscripts read “of Galilee,” which the Union Version follows. “Judea” here is generally taken in the broad sense of the whole land where Jews lived, Galilee included, rather than the southern region alone.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 · The Great Catch; the Paralyzed Man; Levi
chapters.intro: By the lake of Gennesaret Jesus teaches from Simon’s boat and then has the fishermen take a catch that fills two boats; Simon, James and John leave everything and follow him. He heals a man with a skin disease, and forgives and heals a paralyzed man let down through a roof. He calls the tax collector Levi, and answers why he eats with sinners and why his disciples do not fast.

verses.en: Now it happened that, while the crowd was pressing in on him and hearing the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret,

cmp.note: 马可福音和马太福音把这片水叫「加利利海」，路加一律叫「湖」（limnē），这里用的是湖西岸一片平原的名字。指的是同一个湖。
cmp.en: Mark and Matthew call this water "the Sea of Galilee"; Luke always calls it a "lake" (limnē), here named after the plain on its western shore. It is the same lake.

verses.en: and he saw two boats standing by the lake; but the fishermen had gotten out of them and were washing the nets.
And getting into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, he asked him to put out a little from the land; and sitting down, he was teaching the crowds from the boat.
And when he had stopped speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.”
And Simon answered and said, “Master, having toiled through the whole night we took nothing; but at your word I will let down the nets.”

cmp.note: 这是路加福音特有的称呼，意思是「主管、师傅」，别的福音书写「老师」（didaskale）或「拉比」的地方，路加常用这个词。白话都写「老师」，英文写 Master，和合本写「夫子」。
cmp.en: A form of address found only in Luke, meaning "overseer, master"; Luke often uses it where the other Gospels have "Teacher" (didaskale) or "Rabbi." The plain Chinese writes 老师 (lǎoshī, "teacher") for all of them, the English "Master," and the Union Version 夫子 (fūzǐ, "master, teacher").

verses.en: And having done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were breaking.
And they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them; and they came and filled both the boats, so that they began to sink.
But seeing it, Simon Peter fell down at Jesus’s knees, saying, “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.”
For amazement had seized him and all who were with him at the catch of fish that they had taken,
and likewise also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching people.”

cmp.note: 字面是「你将要活捉人」，zōgreō 指把猎物活着捉住。马可福音 1:17 的说法是「成为人的渔夫」，两处希腊文不同。和合本这里写「你要得人了」。
cmp.en: Literally "you will be taking people alive"; zōgreō means to capture alive. Mark 1:17 says "become fishers of people"; the Greek of the two differs. The Union Version has 你要得人了 (nǐ yào dé rén le, "you will gain people").

verses.en: And having brought the boats to land, they left everything and followed him.

And it happened, while he was in one of the towns, that there was a man full of a skin disease; and seeing Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying, “I am willing; be made clean.” And immediately the skin disease left him.
And he charged him to tell no one, “but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

cmp.note: 原文前半句是转述（「吩咐他不要告诉任何人」），后半句没有交代就变成了耶稣的原话。白话补了「又说」，英文照原文直接接上引语。
cmp.en: The Greek begins as reported speech ("charged him to tell no one") and then, without a marker, turns into Jesus’s own words. The Chinese supplies 又说 (yòu shuō, "and said"); the English follows the Greek and simply runs into the quotation.

verses.en: But the word about him was spreading all the more, and many crowds were coming together to hear and to be healed of their sicknesses;
but he himself would withdraw into the deserted places and pray.

And it happened on one of those days that he was teaching, and there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was with him to heal.
And look, men carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were trying to bring him in and lay him before him.
And not finding a way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and let him down through the tiles with his little bed into the middle, in front of Jesus.

cmp.note: 路加说的是「从瓦片中间」；马可福音 2:4 说的是把屋顶「挖开一个洞」。两卷书各照原文译，没有拉齐。
cmp.en: Luke says "through the tiles"; Mark 2:4 says they "dug through" the roof. Each Gospel is translated as it stands, without harmonizing.

verses.en: And seeing their faith, he said, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”

cmp.note: 原文的称呼是「人啊」，白话写「朋友」；马可福音 2:5 这里是「孩子」。和合本没有译出这个称呼，补了「对瘫子」。
cmp.en: The Greek address is "Man"; the plain Chinese writes 朋友 (péngyou, "friend"). Mark 2:5 has "Child" here. The Union Version leaves the address out and supplies 对瘫子 (duì tānzi, "to the paralytic").

verses.en: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
But Jesus, perceiving their reasonings, answered and said to them, “Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man, “I say to you, get up, and taking your little bed, go to your home.”
And immediately, rising up before them, he took what he had been lying on and went off to his home, glorifying God.
And astonishment seized them all, and they were glorifying God, and they were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”
And after these things he went out and noticed a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, “Follow me.”
And leaving everything, he got up and was following him.
And Levi made a great feast for him in his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining at table with them.
And the Pharisees and their scribes were grumbling at his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
And Jesus answered and said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a doctor, but those who are sick;
I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.”
And they said to him, “The disciples of John fast often and offer prayers, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink.”
And he said to them, “Can you make the sons of the wedding hall fast while the bridegroom is with them?

cmp.note: 字面是「婚房的儿子们」，指参加婚礼、陪着新郎的宾客。白话写「来喝喜酒的宾客」，英文照字面，和合本写「陪伴之人」。
cmp.en: Literally "the sons of the wedding hall," meaning the guests who attend the bridegroom. The plain Chinese writes 来喝喜酒的宾客 (lái hē xǐjiǔ de bīnkè, "guests come to the wedding feast"), the English stays literal, and the Union Version has 陪伴之人 (péibàn zhī rén, "the companions").

verses.en: But days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast in those days.”
And he was also telling them a parable: “No one tears a patch from a new garment and puts it on an old garment; otherwise he will both tear the new, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be spilled, and the skins will be destroyed.
But new wine must be put into new wineskins.
And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is good.’”

chapters.title: Chapter 6 · Sabbath Disputes; the Twelve; the Sermon on the Plain
chapters.intro: Two Sabbaths: the disciples pluck grain, and Jesus heals a withered hand; the scribes and Pharisees discuss what to do to him. After a night of prayer he chooses twelve apostles, comes down to a level place, and speaks at length to his disciples: who is blessed and who is not, love your enemies, do not judge, and do what you hear. From verse 20 to the end almost everything is Jesus speaking.

verses.en: Now it happened on a Sabbath that he was passing through grainfields, and his disciples were plucking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands.
But some of the Pharisees said, “Why are you doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?”
And Jesus answered them and said, “Have you not read even this, what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him:
how he entered the house of God and, taking the loaves of the presentation, ate and gave to those with him, which it is not permitted to eat except for the priests alone?”
And he was saying to them, “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
And it happened on another Sabbath that he entered the synagogue and was teaching; and a man was there, and his right hand was withered.
And the scribes and the Pharisees were watching him closely, whether he heals on the Sabbath, so that they might find a charge against him.
But he knew their reasonings, and he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Get up and stand in the middle.” And he rose and stood.
And Jesus said to them, “I ask you whether it is permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to destroy it?”
And looking around at them all, he said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” And he did so, and his hand was restored.
But they were filled with senseless fury, and were discussing with one another what they might do to Jesus.

cmp.note: 这个词字面是「没有理智」，指气昏了头；和合本译「满心大怒」。
cmp.en: The word literally means "mindlessness," rage that has lost its senses; the Union Version has 满心大怒 (mǎnxīn dànù, "filled with great anger").

verses.en: Now it happened in those days that he went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night in prayer to God.
And when day came, he called his disciples to him and chose from them twelve, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
and Matthew and Thomas, and James son of Alphaeus, and Simon who was called the Zealot,
and Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

cmp.note: 马可福音 3:18 和马太福音 10:3 的名单里，这个位置上的名字是「达太」；路加的名单里是「雅各的（儿子）犹大」。各照原文译，没有拉齐。
cmp.en: In the lists at Mark 3:18 and Matthew 10:3 the name in this position is Thaddaeus; Luke’s list has "Judas of James." Each is translated as it stands, without harmonizing.

verses.en: And coming down with them, he stood on a level place, and there was a large crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the coast of Tyre and Sidon,
who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases; and those who were troubled by unclean spirits were being healed.
And all the crowd were seeking to touch him, for power was coming out from him and healing them all.
And lifting up his eyes on his disciples, he was saying: “Blessed are the poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.

cmp.note: 路加这里只说「贫穷的人」，而且是对着听的人说「你们的」；马太福音 5:3 是「心灵贫穷的人」，说的是「他们的」。两处希腊文不同，各照原文译。
cmp.en: Luke says simply "the poor" and addresses the hearers ("yours"); Matthew 5:3 has "the poor in spirit" and "theirs." The Greek differs, and each is translated as it stands.

verses.en: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and revile you and cast out your name as evil on account of the Son of Man.
Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for look, your reward is great in heaven; for their fathers did the same things to the prophets.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your comfort.
Woe to you who are full now, for you will hunger. Woe, you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe when all people speak well of you, for their fathers did the same things to the false prophets.
But I say to you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
To the one who strikes you on the cheek, offer the other also; and from the one who takes away your cloak, do not withhold your tunic either.
Give to everyone who asks you, and from the one who takes away what is yours, do not demand it back.
And as you wish that people would do to you, do likewise to them.
And if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.

cmp.note: charis 本义是「恩惠、好意」，这里指「值得感谢、值得称赞的地方」。和合本译「有什么可酬谢的」；马太福音 5:46 的同一句话用的是另一个词「报酬」。
cmp.en: Charis basically means "favor, goodwill"; here it is "something to your credit." The Union Version has 有什么可酬谢的 (yǒu shénme kě chóuxiè de, "what is there to be thanked for"); the parallel at Matthew 5:46 uses a different word, "reward."

verses.en: And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, so that they may receive back the same amount.
But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he is kind to the ungrateful and the evil.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
And do not judge, and you will not be judged; and do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Pardon, and you will be pardoned;
give, and it will be given to you; a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over, they will give into your lap. For with the measure you measure, it will be measured back to you.”

cmp.note: 「怀里」指把外衣的前襟兜起来做成的口袋，当时的人用它装粮食。说的是买卖粮食时把量器装满、按实、摇紧、再堆到冒尖。
cmp.en: The "lap" is the fold of the outer garment gathered up as a pocket, which people used for carrying grain. The picture is of a grain measure filled, pressed down, shaken and heaped until it overflows.

verses.en: And he also told them a parable: “Can a blind person guide a blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not above the teacher, but everyone, when fully trained, will be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam that is in your own eye?

How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take out the speck that is in your eye,’ when you yourself do not see the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take out the speck that is in your brother’s eye.

cmp.note: 这个词本来指戏台上的演员，引申为装出一副样子给人看的人。和合本译「假冒为善的人」，白话写「装模作样的人」。
cmp.en: The word originally meant a stage actor, and by extension someone who puts on a show for others. The Union Version has 假冒为善的人 (jiǎmào wéi shàn de rén, "one who feigns goodness"); the plain Chinese writes 装模作样的人 (zhuāngmú-zuòyàng de rén, "one who puts on an act").

verses.en: For there is no good tree that bears bad fruit, nor again a bad tree that bears good fruit;
for each tree is known by its own fruit. For they do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they pick grapes from a bramble bush.
The good person out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth good, and the evil person out of the evil brings forth evil; for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks.
And why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I say?
Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show you what he is like:

he is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock; and when a flood came, the river burst against that house and could not shake it, because it had been built well.

cmp.note: 本站的底本这里是「因为它盖得好」；多数抄本是「因为根基立在磐石上」（和马太福音 7:25 一样），和合本跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "because it had been built well"; most manuscripts read "for it had been founded on the rock" (as in Matthew 7:25), which the Union Version follows with 因为根基立在磐石上 (yīnwèi gēnjī lì zài pánshí shàng, "because its foundation was set on the rock").

verses.en: But the one who heard and did not do is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation, against which the river burst, and immediately it collapsed, and the ruin of that house was great.”

chapters.title: Chapter 7 · A Centurion’s Slave; a Widow’s Son; John’s Question; the Woman with the Perfume
chapters.intro: In Capernaum Jesus heals a centurion’s slave from a distance, and at Nain he brings a widow’s only son back to life. John the Baptist sends to ask whether he is "the one who is to come"; Jesus answers and then speaks to the crowds about John. Last, in a Pharisee’s house, a woman known as a sinner wets his feet with her tears and anoints them, and he tells her that her sins are forgiven.

verses.en: When he had completed all his sayings in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.
Now a certain centurion’s slave, who was highly valued by him, was sick and about to die.
And having heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his slave.

cmp.note: 路加说百夫长先托长老、再托朋友来传话，自己没有露面；马太福音 8:5–13 讲同一件事，说的是百夫长自己来见耶稣。各照原文译，没有拉齐。
cmp.en: Luke has the centurion send elders and then friends, never appearing himself; Matthew 8:5–13 tells the same event with the centurion coming to Jesus in person. Each is translated as it stands, without harmonizing.

verses.en: And when they came to Jesus, they were pleading with him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to grant this to him,
for he loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us.”

And Jesus was going with them. But when he was already not far from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to him, “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not fit to have you come under my roof;
therefore I did not even count myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant be healed.

cmp.note: 前面第 2、3 节和后面第 10 节叙述里用的词是 doulos（奴仆），百夫长自己说话时用的是 pais，既可以指仆人，也可以指孩子，口气亲近一些。白话分别写「奴仆」「仆人」。
cmp.en: The narration in verses 2, 3 and 10 uses doulos ("slave"); the centurion himself says pais, which can mean a servant or a child and sounds warmer. The plain Chinese writes 奴仆 (núpú, "slave") and 仆人 (púrén, "servant") accordingly.

verses.en: For I too am a man set under authority, having soldiers under me, and I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
And hearing these things, Jesus marveled at him, and turning to the crowd following him he said, “I say to you, not even in Israel have I found such faith.”
And when those who had been sent returned to the house, they found the slave in good health.
And it happened soon afterward that he went to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd were going with him.
And as he drew near to the gate of the town, look, a man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a considerable crowd from the town was with her.
And seeing her, the Lord was moved with compassion for her and said to her, “Do not weep.”

cmp.note: 路加在叙述里常常直接把耶稣叫作「主」，这是第一处；马可福音和马太福音的叙述里几乎不这样叫。
cmp.en: Luke’s narration often calls Jesus simply "the Lord," and this is the first instance; the narration in Mark and Matthew almost never does.

verses.en: And coming forward, he touched the bier, and the bearers stood still; and he said, “Young man, I say to you, arise.”
And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother.
And fear seized them all, and they were glorifying God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and, “God has visited his people.”
And this report about him went out in the whole of Judea and all the surrounding region.
And John’s disciples reported to him about all these things. And calling to him two of his disciples, John
sent them to the Lord, saying, “Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?”
And when the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for another?’”
In that hour he healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many who were blind he granted sight.

And he answered and said to them, “Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, those with skin diseases are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news proclaimed to them.
And blessed is whoever does not stumble because of me.”
And when John’s messengers had gone, he began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who are in splendid clothing and live in luxury are in the royal palaces.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written, ‘Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.’

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《玛拉基书》3:1（并《出埃及记》23:20）。马可福音开头（1:2）也引了这一句。
cmp.en: The quotation is from Malachi 3:1 (with Exodus 23:20). Mark quotes the same line at its opening (1:2).

verses.en: I say to you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
And all the people who heard, and the tax collectors, acknowledged God to be right, having been baptized with the baptism of John;

cmp.note: 字面是「以上帝为义」，意思是承认上帝做得对。底本把第 29、30 两节放在括号里，表示这是叙述者插进来的说明，不是耶稣的话；也有人把这两节读成耶稣接着说的话。本站的圆括号只用来放补的字，所以这里没有用括号，只在第 28 节末收了引号。
cmp.en: Literally "they justified God," that is, acknowledged that God was right. The edition puts verses 29 and 30 in parentheses, marking them as the narrator’s aside rather than Jesus’s words; some read them instead as a continuation of what Jesus says. This site reserves parentheses in the Chinese for supplied words, so none are used here; the quotation is simply closed at the end of verse 28.

verses.en: but the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the purpose of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
“To what then shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?
They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling to one another, who say, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’
For John the Baptist has come eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’
And wisdom is shown to be right by all her children.”

cmp.note: 路加这里是「凭她所有的儿女」；马太福音 11:19 本站的底本是「凭它做出的事」。和合本这里写「智慧之子都以智慧为是」。这句话像一句俗语，经文没有解释。
cmp.en: Luke has "by all her children"; at Matthew 11:19 this site’s edition reads "by her works." The Union Version here has 智慧之子都以智慧为是 (zhìhuì zhī zǐ dōu yǐ zhìhuì wéi shì, "the children of wisdom all hold wisdom to be right"). The saying sounds like a proverb, and the text does not explain it.

verses.en: Now one of the Pharisees was asking him to eat with him, and entering the Pharisee’s house, he reclined at table.
And look, a woman who was a sinner in the town, having learned that he was reclining at table in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of perfume,
and standing behind him at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears and was wiping them with the hair of her head, and was kissing his feet and anointing them with the perfume.
And seeing this, the Pharisee who had invited him said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what kind of woman this is who is touching him, that she is a sinner.”
And Jesus answered and said to him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” And he says, “Teacher, say it.”
“A certain moneylender had two debtors; one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
When they could not repay, he forgave them both. So which of them will love him more?”
Simon answered and said, “I suppose the one to whom he forgave more.” And he said to him, “You have judged rightly.”
And turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in she has not stopped kissing my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfume.
For this reason, I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much; but the one to whom little is forgiven loves little.”

cmp.note: 「因为她爱得多」这半句有两种读法：一是她的爱是罪被赦免的原因，二是她的爱证明她的罪已经被赦免（和前面欠债的比方一致）。原文两种都说得通，白话照字面译，没有取舍。
cmp.en: The clause "for she loved much" can be read two ways: her love is the reason she is forgiven, or her love is the evidence that she has been forgiven (which fits the story of the two debtors). The Greek allows both, and the translation stays literal without choosing.

verses.en: And he said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
And those reclining at table with him began to say among themselves, “Who is this, who even forgives sins?”
But he said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

chapters.title: Chapter 8 · The Sower; the Storm Stilled; Legion; Jairus’s Daughter
chapters.intro: Jesus travels from town to town with the twelve and a group of women who provide for them. He tells the parable of the sower and explains it to his disciples: the seed is the word of God. On the lake he rebukes a storm and it stops; among the Gerasenes he drives many demons out of a man and into a herd of pigs; back across, he heals a woman with a flow of blood and raises the dead daughter of Jairus.

verses.en: And it happened soon afterward that he was traveling through town and village, proclaiming and bringing the good news of the kingdom of God; and the twelve were with him,
and some women who had been healed of evil spirits and sicknesses: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
and Joanna the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, who were providing for them out of their own possessions.
And when a large crowd was gathering and people from town after town were making their way to him, he spoke by means of a parable:
“The sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and it was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it up.
And other seed fell on the rock, and when it grew up it withered, because it had no moisture.
And other seed fell in the midst of the thorns, and the thorns grew up with it and choked it.
And other seed fell into the good soil, and when it grew up it produced fruit a hundredfold.” Saying these things, he was calling out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
And his disciples were asking him what this parable might mean.
And he said, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to the rest in parables, so that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’

cmp.note: 单引号里的话引自旧约《以赛亚书》6:9，那里是上帝对先知以赛亚说的，讲的是百姓听了也不肯明白。马可福音 4:12 引得更长，多了「免得他们回转过来，得到赦免」。
cmp.en: The words in single quotation marks are from Isaiah 6:9, where God is speaking to the prophet about a people who hear and refuse to understand. Mark 4:12 quotes more of the passage, adding "lest they turn back and it be forgiven them."

verses.en: Now the parable is this: the seed is the word of God.
And those beside the road are the ones who have heard; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, so that they may not believe and be saved.
And those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root; they believe for a time, and in a time of testing they fall away.
And what fell among the thorns, these are the ones who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked by the cares and riches and pleasures of life, and they bring no fruit to maturity.
And what is in the good soil, these are the ones who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, hold it fast and bear fruit with endurance.
Now no one, having lit a lamp, covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed, but puts it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
For there is nothing hidden that will not become visible, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light.
So take care how you hear; for whoever has, to him more will be given, and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”

cmp.note: 路加写的是「他自以为有的」；马可福音 4:25 的同一句话是「他有的」。
cmp.en: Luke writes "what he thinks he has"; the same saying at Mark 4:25 has simply "what he has."

verses.en: And his mother and brothers came to him, and they were not able to reach him because of the crowd.
And it was reported to him, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”
But he answered and said to them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”
Now it happened on one of those days that he got into a boat, he and his disciples, and he said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.” And they set out.
And as they were sailing he fell asleep. And a windstorm came down on the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger.
And coming to him, they woke him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” And having woken, he rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they ceased, and there was a calm.
And he said to them, “Where is your faith?” And being afraid, they marveled, saying to one another, “Who then is this, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”
And they sailed down to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.
And as he stepped out on land, there met him a certain man from the town who had demons; and for a long time he had worn no clothing, and he was not living in a house but among the tombs.
And seeing Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him and said with a loud voice, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me.”

For he had been commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For many times it had seized him, and he was kept under guard, bound with chains and shackles, and breaking the bonds he would be driven by the demon into the deserted places.
And Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.

cmp.note: 这是从拉丁文借来的词，指罗马军队的一个军团，满编有五六千人。和合本译成「群」。
cmp.en: A word borrowed from Latin for a legion of the Roman army, five to six thousand men at full strength. The Union Version translates it 群 (qún, "a crowd").

verses.en: And they were begging him not to command them to go away into the abyss.
Now a herd of many pigs was feeding there on the mountain, and they begged him to permit them to enter those; and he permitted them.
And the demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
And seeing what had happened, the herdsmen fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside.

And they went out to see what had happened, and they came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
And those who had seen it reported to them how the demon-possessed man had been saved.
And all the people of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked him to depart from them, for they were gripped with great fear; and getting into a boat, he returned.
And the man from whom the demons had gone out was begging to be with him; but he sent him away, saying,
“Return to your home, and tell how much God has done for you.” And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole town how much Jesus had done for him.
Now when Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
And look, there came a man whose name was Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue; and falling at the feet of Jesus, he was pleading with him to come to his house,
because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. And as he went, the crowds were pressing in on him.
And a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians and could not be healed by anyone,

cmp.note: 「在医生身上花光了全部家当」这半句，有几份早期抄本没有；本站的底本与和合本都收了。
cmp.en: The clause "who had spent all her living on physicians" is missing from a few early manuscripts; both this site’s edition and the Union Version include it.

verses.en: came up behind and touched the fringe of his garment, and immediately her flow of blood stopped.

cmp.note: 指犹太男子外衣四角上缝的穗子（旧约《民数记》15:38 规定的）。马可福音 5:27 只说她摸了「衣服」。
cmp.en: The tassels sewn on the four corners of a Jewish man’s outer garment, as required by Numbers 15:38. Mark 5:27 says only that she touched his "garment."

verses.en: And Jesus said, “Who is it that touched me?” And when all were denying it, Peter said, “Master, the crowds are hemming you in and pressing against you.”
But Jesus said, “Someone touched me, for I perceived that power had gone out from me.”

And seeing that she had not escaped notice, the woman came trembling, and falling down before him she declared in the presence of all the people why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
And he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
While he is still speaking, someone comes from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter has died; trouble the Teacher no longer.”
But Jesus, hearing it, answered him, “Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be saved.”
And coming to the house, he did not allow anyone to go in with him except Peter and John and James, and the father of the child and the mother.
And all were weeping and beating their breasts for her. But he said, “Do not weep, for she has not died but is sleeping.”
And they were laughing at him, knowing that she had died.
But he, taking her by the hand, called out, saying, “Child, arise.”

cmp.note: 马可福音 5:41 在这里保留了耶稣的亚兰话原句「大利大，古米」，再翻成希腊文；路加只写了希腊文。
cmp.en: Mark 5:41 preserves Jesus’s Aramaic words here, "Talitha koum," and then translates them; Luke gives only the Greek.

verses.en: And her spirit returned, and she got up immediately; and he directed that something be given her to eat.
And her parents were amazed; but he charged them to tell no one what had happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 · Five Loaves and Two Fish; Peter’s Answer; the Transfiguration; Toward Jerusalem
chapters.intro: Jesus sends the twelve out to proclaim and to heal, and Herod, hearing of it, is perplexed. He feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish; Peter calls him the Christ, and Jesus at once foretells that he must suffer, be killed and be raised. On a mountain his appearance changes; coming down, he heals a boy seized by a spirit. Last, he sets out resolutely for Jerusalem and on the road speaks of what following him costs.

verses.en: And calling the twelve together, he gave them power and authority over all the demons and to heal diseases,
and he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick,
and he said to them, “Take nothing for the road, neither staff nor bag nor bread nor silver, nor have two tunics apiece.

cmp.note: 路加这里说连手杖也不带（马太福音 10:10 相同）；马可福音 6:8 说的是「除了一根手杖，什么都不要带」。各照原文译，没有拉齐。
cmp.en: Luke says not even a staff (as does Matthew 10:10); Mark 6:8 says "nothing except a staff only." Each is translated as it stands, without harmonizing.

verses.en: And whatever house you enter, stay there, and from there go out.
And as for all who do not receive you, when you go out from that town shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.”
And going out, they were passing through the villages, bringing the good news and healing everywhere.
Now Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, and he was greatly perplexed, because it was said by some that John had been raised from the dead,

cmp.note: 字面是「管四分之一的人」，罗马人给小块属地统治者的头衔，地位比王低。马可福音 6:14 把他叫作「希律王」。和合本这里译「分封的王」。
cmp.en: Literally "ruler of a fourth part," a Roman title for the ruler of a small dependent territory, ranking below a king. Mark 6:14 calls him "King Herod." The Union Version here has 分封的王 (fēnfēng de wáng, "enfeoffed king").

verses.en: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the prophets of old had risen.
But Herod said, “John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things?” And he was seeking to see him.
And when the apostles returned, they told him all that they had done. And taking them along, he withdrew privately to a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds, learning of it, followed him; and welcoming them, he was speaking to them about the kingdom of God, and he was healing those who had need of healing.

Now the day began to decline, and the twelve came and said to him, “Send the crowd away, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms and find lodging and get provisions, for we are here in a deserted place.”
But he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” And they said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people.”
For there were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, “Have them recline in groups of about fifty each.”
And they did so and had them all recline.
And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed them and broke them, and he was giving them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
And they all ate and were filled; and what was left over to them was taken up, twelve baskets of broken pieces.
And it happened, while he was praying alone, that the disciples were with him, and he asked them, saying, “Who do the crowds say that I am?”
And they answered and said, “John the Baptist; but others, Elijah; and others, that one of the prophets of old has risen.”
And he said to them, “But you, who do you say that I am?” And Peter answered and said, “The Christ of God.”

cmp.note: 路加这里是「上帝的基督」；马可福音 8:29 只是「你是基督」，马太福音 16:16 是「你是基督，是永生上帝的儿子」。和合本这里写「是神所立的基督」，「所立的」是补的。
cmp.en: Luke has "the Christ of God"; Mark 8:29 has only "You are the Christ," and Matthew 16:16 "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." The Union Version here writes 是神所立的基督 (shì Shén suǒ lì de Jīdū, "the Christ appointed by God"), where "appointed" is supplied.

verses.en: But he, sternly warning them, charged them to tell this to no one,
saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.”
And he was saying to all, “If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.

cmp.note: 「天天」这个词只有路加有；马可福音 8:34 和马太福音 16:24 的同一句话没有。
cmp.en: The word "daily" is found only in Luke; the same saying at Mark 8:34 and Matthew 16:24 lacks it.

verses.en: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake, this one will save it.
For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world and lose or forfeit himself?
For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed when he comes in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels.
But I tell you truly, there are some of those standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.”

cmp.note: 别的福音书在这里用的是希伯来话的「阿们，我告诉你们」（本站写「我实在告诉你们」）；路加这里把「阿们」换成了希腊文的「真实地」，意思一样。
cmp.en: The other Gospels have the Hebrew "Amen, I say to you" here (which this site renders "Truly I say to you"); Luke replaces "Amen" with the Greek adverb "truly," with the same meaning.

verses.en: Now it happened about eight days after these sayings that, taking along Peter and John and James, he went up on the mountain to pray.

cmp.note: 路加说「大约八天」；马可福音 9:2 和马太福音 17:1 说「过了六天」。各照原文译。
cmp.en: Luke says "about eight days"; Mark 9:2 and Matthew 17:1 say "after six days." Each is translated as it stands.

verses.en: And it happened, while he was praying, that the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing became white, flashing like lightning.
And look, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
who, appearing in glory, were speaking of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.

cmp.note: exodos 字面是「出去、离开」，这里指耶稣的死；这个词也是旧约《出埃及记》的希腊文书名。和合本译「去世」。这一节只有路加有。
cmp.en: Exodos literally means "a going out, departure," here Jesus’s death; it is also the Greek title of the book of Exodus. The Union Version has 去世 (qùshì, "passing away"). Only Luke has this verse.

verses.en: Now Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; but having become fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

And it happened, as they were parting from him, that Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he was saying.
And while he was saying these things, a cloud came and was overshadowing them; and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my Son, the Chosen One; listen to him.”

cmp.note: 路加这里是「我所拣选的」；马可福音 9:7 是「我亲爱的儿子」。较晚的抄本把路加这里也改成了「亲爱的」，本站的底本与和合本都作「拣选的」。
cmp.en: Luke has "the Chosen One"; Mark 9:7 has "my beloved Son." Later manuscripts changed Luke to "beloved" as well; this site’s edition and the Union Version both read "chosen."

verses.en: And when the voice had come, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent and in those days reported to no one anything of what they had seen.
Now it happened on the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, that a large crowd met him.
And look, a man from the crowd cried out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look upon my son, for he is my only child;
and look, a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it convulses him with foaming, and it scarcely leaves him, bruising him.
And I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they could not.”
And Jesus answered and said, “O faithless and twisted generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”
But while he was still approaching, the demon threw him down and convulsed him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and gave him back to his father.
And all were astonished at the majesty of God. But while all were marveling at everything he was doing, he said to his disciples,
“Let these words sink into your ears: for the Son of Man is about to be handed over into the hands of men.”
But they did not understand this saying, and it was concealed from them so that they might not perceive it; and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
And an argument arose among them as to which of them was the greatest.
But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their heart, took a little child and stood him beside himself,
and said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me; for the one who is least among you all, this one is great.”
And John answered and said, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we were trying to stop him, because he does not follow with us.”
But Jesus said to him, “Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you.”
Now it happened, as the days for his being taken up were being fulfilled, that he set his face to go to Jerusalem,

cmp.note: 字面是「把脸定住」，意思是拿定了主意、不再回头。这卷书从这里起有很长的一段（一直到第 19 章）都在讲耶稣走向耶路撒冷的路上发生的事，其中许多内容只有路加福音有。
cmp.en: Literally "he set his face," that is, made up his mind and would not turn back. From here a long stretch of the book (through chapter 19) tells what happens on the way to Jerusalem, much of it found only in Luke.

verses.en: and he sent messengers ahead of him. And going, they entered a village of the Samaritans to make preparations for him;
and they did not receive him, because his face was set toward Jerusalem.
And seeing this, the disciples James and John said, “Lord, do you want us to tell fire to come down from heaven and consume them?”
But turning, he rebuked them.

cmp.note: 本站的底本这一节到「责备了他们」就结束，下一节只有「他们就往另一个村子去了」。和合本这两节里的「你们的心如何，你们并不知道」和「人子来不是要灭人的性命，是要救人的性命」，只见于较晚的抄本，一般认为是后来加进去的。
cmp.en: In this site’s edition the verse ends at "he rebuked them," and the next verse is only "And they went on to another village." The words the Union Version has in these two verses, "You do not know what manner of spirit you are of" and "For the Son of Man did not come to destroy people’s lives but to save them," are found only in later manuscripts and are generally regarded as additions.

verses.en: And they went on to another village.
And as they were going along the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go.”
And Jesus said to him, “Foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
And he said to another, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”
But he said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but you, go and announce the kingdom of God.”
And another also said, “I will follow you, Lord; but first permit me to say farewell to those at my home.”
But Jesus said, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”

chapters.title: Chapter 10 · The Seventy-Two; the Samaritan; Martha and Mary
chapters.intro: Jesus sends out seventy-two more people in pairs, telling them how to enter a town and stay in a house; they come back reporting that even the demons submit to them. A lawyer asks who his neighbor is, and Jesus tells of a Samaritan who helps a man beaten by robbers. Last, he is a guest in the home of the sisters Martha and Mary. Verses 2 to 16 are all Jesus speaking.

verses.en: Now after these things the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of him into every town and place where he himself was about to come.

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「七十二」，另有许多抄本是「七十」，和合本跟的是后一种。第 17 节相同。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "seventy-two"; many other manuscripts read "seventy," which the Union Version follows with 七十个人 (qīshí gè rén, "seventy people"). The same holds for verse 17.

verses.en: And he was saying to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few; therefore ask the lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
Go; look, I am sending you out as lambs in the midst of wolves.
Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals; and greet no one along the road.
And whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’
And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; but if not, it will return upon you.

cmp.note: 字面是「平安之子」，希伯来式的说法，指配得这平安的人。
cmp.en: Literally "a son of peace," a Hebrew way of saying a person fit to receive that peace.
