verses.en: And stay in that same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house.
And whatever town you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you,
and heal the sick in it, and say to them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’
But whatever town you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say,
‘Even the dust from your town that clings to our feet we wipe off against you; nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God has come near.’
I say to you that it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
Nevertheless it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You will be brought down to Hades.

cmp.note: 底本是一句问话：「你难道要被高举到天上吗？」和合本的「你已经升到天上」跟的是另一种读法。
cmp.en: The edition reads a question, "will you be exalted to heaven?"; the Union Version’s 你已经升到天上 (nǐ yǐjīng shēng dào tiānshàng, "you have already risen to heaven") follows a different reading.

verses.en: The one who hears you hears me, and the one who rejects you rejects me; and the one who rejects me rejects the one who sent me.”
Now the seventy-two returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.”
And he said to them, “I was watching Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
Look, I have given you the authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will ever harm you.
Nevertheless do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in the heavens.”

In that same hour he rejoiced greatly in the Holy Spirit and said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to infants; yes, Father, for such was your good pleasure.
All things have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.”
And turning to the disciples he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
For I say to you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.”
And look, a certain lawyer stood up to test him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
And he said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
And he answered and said, “ ‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind,’ and ‘your neighbor as yourself.’ ”

cmp.note: 前一句引自旧约《申命记》6:5，后一句引自《利未记》19:18。
cmp.en: The first part quotes Deuteronomy 6:5 and the second Leviticus 19:18.

verses.en: And he said to him, “You have answered rightly; do this, and you will live.”
But he, wanting to justify himself, said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Taking this up, Jesus said, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who stripped him and beat him and went away, leaving him half dead.
Now by chance a certain priest was going down that road, and seeing him he passed by on the other side.
And likewise also a Levite, coming to the place and seeing him, passed by on the other side.
But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came to where he was, and seeing him was moved with compassion,
and coming to him he bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; and setting him on his own animal he brought him to an inn and took care of him.
And on the next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper and said, ‘Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back.’
Which of these three, do you think, became a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
And he said, “The one who showed him mercy.” And Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”
Now as they went on their way, he entered a certain village; and a certain woman named Martha welcomed him.
And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at the feet of Jesus and was listening to his word.
But Martha was distracted with much serving; and she came up and said, “Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her then to help me.”
But the Lord answered and said to her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
but few things are needed, or one; for Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her.”

cmp.w: oligōn de estin chreia ē henos
cmp.note: 底本是「需要的不多，或者只要一样」；多数抄本只有「需要的只有一样」，和合本跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition reads "few things are needed, or one"; most manuscripts have only "one thing is needed," which the Union Version follows with 不可少的只有一件 (bùkě shǎo de zhǐyǒu yī jiàn, "only one thing is indispensable").

chapters.title: Chapter 11 · Teaching on Prayer; the Beelzebul Dispute; Woes to Pharisees and Lawyers
chapters.intro: The disciples ask Jesus to teach them to pray; he gives them a short prayer and, with a story about borrowing bread from a friend at midnight, urges them simply to ask. Some say he casts out demons by the ruler of demons; he answers them, and says this generation will be given only "the sign of Jonah." In the second half he dines at a Pharisee’s house and says "woe to you" six times, against the Pharisees and the lawyers.

verses.en: And it happened that as he was praying in a certain place, when he stopped, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
And he said to them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come;

cmp.note: 这里的祷词比《马太福音》6:9–13 的短。和合本按较长的抄本，多出「我们在天上的」和「愿你的旨意行在地上如同行在天上」，本站的底本没有；一般认为那些是抄写的人照马太福音补齐的。
cmp.en: This prayer is shorter than the one in Matthew 6:9–13. The Union Version follows longer manuscripts and adds 我们在天上的 (wǒmen zài tiānshàng de, "our … who is in heaven") and 愿你的旨意行在地上如同行在天上 (yuàn nǐ de zhǐyì xíng zài dìshàng rútóng xíng zài tiānshàng, "may your will be done on earth as in heaven"), which the edition this site follows lacks; they are generally thought to have been filled in by copyists from Matthew.

verses.en: give us each day our daily bread;

cmp.note: 这个词在别处几乎没有出现过，意思不能确定，通行的理解是「每天需要的」或「明天的」。和合本把「饼」译成「饮食」。
cmp.en: The word occurs almost nowhere else and its meaning is uncertain; the usual renderings are "needed for the day" or "for tomorrow." The Union Version turns "bread" into 饮食 (yǐnshí, "food and drink").

verses.en: and forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us; and do not bring us into temptation.’”

cmp.note: 底本的祷词到这里结束。和合本末尾的「救我们脱离凶恶」见于较长的抄本，是《马太福音》里有的一句。
cmp.en: In the edition the prayer ends here. The Union Version’s closing 救我们脱离凶恶 (jiù wǒmen tuōlí xiōng’è, "deliver us from evil") comes from longer manuscripts and is a line found in Matthew.

verses.en: And he said to them, “Which of you will have a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,
since a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him’;
and that one answers from inside and says, ‘Do not bother me; the door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot get up and give you anything.’
I say to you, even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he will rise and give him as much as he needs.

cmp.note: 字面是「不知羞」，指这人半夜还厚着脸皮来求。和合本译成「情词迫切的直求」。
cmp.en: Literally "shamelessness," of the man who has the nerve to come asking at midnight. The Union Version renders it 情词迫切的直求 (qíngcí pòqiè de zhí qiú, "earnest, insistent asking").

verses.en: And I say to you, ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
And which father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will instead of a fish hand him a snake?
Or if he asks for an egg, will hand him a scorpion?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.”
And he was casting out a demon that was mute; and it happened that when the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds marveled.
But some of them said, “By Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, he casts out the demons”;
and others, testing him, were seeking from him a sign from heaven.
But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.
And if Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out the demons by Beelzebul.
And if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
But if it is by the finger of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

cmp.note: 原文是「上帝的手指」，旧约里的说法（《出埃及记》8:19），指上帝亲自动手；和合本译成「神的能力」。《马太福音》12:28 在同一句话里写的是「上帝的灵」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "the finger of God," an Old Testament phrase (Exodus 8:19) for God acting directly; the Union Version renders it 神的能力 (Shén de nénglì, "the power of God"). In the same saying Matthew 12:28 has "the Spirit of God."

verses.en: When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are in peace;
but when one stronger than he comes upon him and overcomes him, he takes away his full armor in which he trusted and divides his spoils.
The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters.
When the unclean spirit goes out of the person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding it, it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came out’;
and coming, it finds it swept and put in order.
Then it goes and takes along seven other spirits more evil than itself, and entering they dwell there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first.”
Now it happened that as he was saying these things, a certain woman from the crowd raised her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts at which you nursed!”
But he said, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it!”
And as the crowds were gathering more thickly, he began to say, “This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also the Son of Man will be to this generation.

cmp.note: 约拿的事见旧约《约拿书》：上帝派他到外族的大城尼尼微去警告那里的人，他们听了就悔改。
cmp.en: Jonah’s story is in the Old Testament book of Jonah: God sent him to warn the great foreign city of Nineveh, and its people repented when they heard him.

verses.en: The queen of the south will be raised at the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and look, something greater than Jonah is here.
No one, having lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under the measuring basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
The lamp of the body is your eye. When your eye is single, your whole body also is full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
See to it, then, that the light that is in you is not darkness.
If, then, your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its ray gives you light.”
Now as he spoke, a Pharisee asks him to dine with him; and he went in and reclined at table.
And the Pharisee, seeing it, marveled that he did not first wash before the meal.

cmp.note: 原文只说「洗」，指的是饭前照规矩洗手。这是当时法利赛人看重的礼仪上的洁净，不是为了卫生。
cmp.en: The Greek says only "wash"; it means the customary hand-washing before a meal, a matter of ritual purity that the Pharisees valued, not of hygiene.

verses.en: But the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and of the dish, but your inside is full of robbery and wickedness.
Foolish ones! Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?
But give as alms the things that are within, and look, everything is clean for you.
But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe mint and rue and every garden herb, and pass by justice and the love of God; these you ought to have done, without leaving the others aside.
Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the chief seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you, because you are like unmarked tombs, and the people who walk over them do not know it.”

cmp.note: 按犹太律法，碰到坟墓的人就算不洁净（《民数记》19:16），所以坟墓要做记号。
cmp.en: Under Jewish law anyone who touched a grave became unclean (Numbers 19:16), which is why graves were marked.

verses.en: And one of the lawyers answers and says to him, “Teacher, in saying these things you insult us also.”
But he said, “Woe to you lawyers also, because you load people with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
So you are witnesses and you approve of the deeds of your fathers, because they killed them and you build.
Therefore also the Wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,’
so that the blood of all the prophets, poured out since the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house. Yes, I say to you, it will be required of this generation.
Woe to you lawyers, because you took away the key of knowledge; you yourselves did not enter, and those who were entering you hindered.”
And when he went out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to press him hard and to question him closely about many things,
lying in wait for him, to catch something out of his mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 · Do Not Fear, Do Not Worry, Keep Awake
chapters.intro: Jesus first tells his disciples not to fear those who kill the body and to acknowledge him before people. When a man asks him to settle an inheritance, he tells of a rich man busy building bigger barns who dies that very night; then he teaches the disciples not to worry about food and clothing and to stay awake like slaves waiting for their master. He says he has come to bring division, and rebukes the crowds for failing to read the present time.

verses.en: Meanwhile, when the crowd had gathered in the tens of thousands, so that they were trampling one another, he began to say to his disciples first, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
But nothing is covered up that will not be uncovered, and hidden that will not be known.
Therefore whatever you said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you spoke in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
But I say to you, my friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more that they can do.
But I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna; yes, I say to you, fear this one.
Are not five sparrows sold for two assaria? And not one of them is forgotten before God.
But even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.
And I say to you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man also will acknowledge him before the angels of God;
but the one who denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but to the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit it will not be forgiven.
And when they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how or what you are to answer in defense, or what you are to say;
for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say.”
Now someone from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
But he said to him, “Man, who appointed me a judge or divider over you?”
And he said to them, “Watch out, and guard yourselves against all greed, for not in anyone’s abundance does his life consist, from his possessions.”
And he told them a parable, saying, “The land of a certain rich man produced a good crop.
And he was reasoning within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
And he said, ‘This I will do: I will pull down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will gather all my grain and my goods,
and I will say to my soul, Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, be merry.’
But God said to him, ‘Fool! This night they are demanding your soul back from you; and the things you prepared, whose will they be?’

cmp.note: 原文是「他们要向你讨回你的灵魂」，没有说「他们」是谁，是一种不明说主语的讲法。「灵魂」这个词也就是「性命」。
cmp.en: Literally "they are demanding your soul back from you," with no indication of who "they" are, an impersonal way of speaking. The word for "soul" also means "life."

verses.en: So is the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
And he said to his disciples, “Therefore I say to you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on.
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storeroom nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more are you worth than the birds!
And which of you by worrying can add a cubit to his span of life?
If then you cannot do even the least thing, why do you worry about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how they grow: they do not toil or spin; yet I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass in the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more you, you of little faith!
And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be anxious;
for all the nations of the world seek after these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
But seek his kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
Do not fear, little flock, for your Father was pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give alms; make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys;
for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Let your waists be girded and your lamps burning,
and you be like people waiting for their master, whenever he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him immediately.
Blessed are those slaves whom the master, when he comes, will find keeping awake; truly I say to you that he will gird himself and have them recline at table, and will come and serve them.
And if he comes in the second watch, or in the third, and finds them so, blessed are they.
But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be dug through.
You also be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”
And Peter said, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or also to everyone?”
And the Lord said, “Who then is the faithful, wise steward, whom the master will set over his household servants, to give them their ration of food at the proper time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.
I say to you truly, he will set him over all his possessions.
But if that slave says in his heart, ‘My master is delayed in coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and put his portion with the unfaithful.
And that slave who knew his master’s will and did not get ready or act according to his will, will be beaten with many blows;

but the one who did not know, and did things deserving blows, will be beaten with few. And from everyone to whom much was given, much will be sought; and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they will ask the more.
I came to throw fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

cmp.note: 这半句有两种读法：「我多么盼望它已经烧起来」，或者「要是已经烧起来了，我还要什么呢」。白话和英文取前一种，和合本近于后一种。
cmp.en: The clause can be read two ways: "how I wish it were already kindled," or "what more do I want, if it is already kindled?" Both translations here take the first; the Union Version is closer to the second.

verses.en: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how I am pressed until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I came to give peace on the earth? No, I say to you, but rather division.
For from now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three;

they will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against the mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against the mother-in-law.”
And he was saying also to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens;
and when you see a south wind blowing, you say, ‘There will be scorching heat,’ and it happens.
Hypocrites! You know how to discern the face of the earth and of the sky, but how is it that you do not know how to discern this time?
And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For as you are going with your accuser before a ruler, on the way make an effort to be released from him, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I say to you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid even the last lepton.”

chapters.title: Chapter 13 · A Call to Repent; Healing on the Sabbath; the Narrow Door
chapters.intro: People tell Jesus about Galileans killed by Pilate; he says everyone must repent, and tells of a fig tree that has borne no fruit for three years. On a Sabbath he heals a woman bent over for eighteen years and clashes with the ruler of the synagogue. He compares the kingdom of God to a mustard seed and to leaven, and urges people to enter by the narrow door. At the end he laments over Jerusalem.

verses.en: Now there were some present at that very time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

cmp.note: 意思是这些加利利人正在献祭的时候被彼拉多的兵杀了。这件事别处没有记载。
cmp.en: That is, these Galileans were killed by Pilate’s soldiers while they were offering sacrifices. The incident is not recorded elsewhere.

verses.en: And he answered and said to them, “Do you think that these Galileans were sinners beyond all the Galileans, because they have suffered these things?
No, I say to you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.
Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they were debtors beyond all the people who live in Jerusalem?
No, I say to you; but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
And he was telling this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and did not find any.
And he said to the vinedresser, ‘Look, for three years I have been coming seeking fruit on this fig tree and I find none. Cut it down; why should it even use up the ground?’
But he answers and says to him, ‘Master, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put on manure;
and if it bears fruit in the coming year—but if not, you will cut it down.’”

cmp.note: 原文前半句没有说完：「以后要是结果子——」，后面该接的「那就好」「就留着」没有写出来。和合本补了「便罢」，白话把补的字放在括号里，英文照原样留着半句。
cmp.en: The first half of the sentence is left unfinished in the Greek: "and if it bears fruit in the coming year—" with the expected "well and good" unsaid. The Union Version supplies 便罢 (biàn bà, "then fine"); the plain Chinese puts the supplied words in parentheses, and the English leaves the sentence broken off.

verses.en: Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
And look, a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; and she was bent over and unable to straighten up at all.
And seeing her, Jesus called to her and said to her, “Woman, you are released from your infirmity,”
and he laid his hands on her; and at once she was made straight, and she was glorifying God.

But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, answered and was saying to the crowd, “There are six days in which work ought to be done; so come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.”
But the Lord answered him and said, “Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?
And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for, look, eighteen years—ought she not to be released from this bond on the Sabbath day?”
And as he said these things, all his opponents were being put to shame, and the whole crowd was rejoicing at all the glorious things being done by him.
He was saying therefore, “What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and threw into his own garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.”
And again he said, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until it was all leavened.”
And he was passing through towns and villages one after another, teaching and making his way toward Jerusalem.
And someone said to him, “Lord, are those who are being saved few?” And he said to them,
“Strive to enter through the narrow door, because many, I say to you, will seek to enter and will not be able,

once the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, open to us’; and he will answer and say to you, ‘I do not know where you are from.’
Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets’;
and he will say to you, ‘I do not know where you are from; depart from me, all you workers of unrighteousness.’
There will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves being thrown out.
And they will come from east and west and from north and south and will recline at table in the kingdom of God.
And look, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.”
In that very hour some Pharisees came up, saying to him, “Get out and go on from here, because Herod wants to kill you.”
And he said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am finished.

cmp.note: 这个词可以是「我完成了」，也可以是「我被成全」「我到了终点」。和合本译「我的事就成全了」。
cmp.en: The word can mean "I finish," or "I am brought to completion," "I reach my goal." The Union Version has 我的事就成全了 (wǒ de shì jiù chéngquán le, "my work will be completed").

verses.en: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, because it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.’
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her—how often I wanted to gather your children, the way a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
Look, your house is left to you. And I say to you, you will certainly not see me until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

cmp.note: 这句话引自旧约《诗篇》118:26。
cmp.en: The words quote Psalm 118:26.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 · A Sabbath Dinner; the Great Banquet; the Cost of Discipleship
chapters.intro: On a Sabbath Jesus dines at the house of a leading Pharisee and heals a man with dropsy. He advises the guests not to grab the places of honor and the host to invite those who cannot pay him back, and tells of a man who gives a great dinner while every invited guest makes an excuse. Afterward he tells the crowds traveling with him that to be his disciple one must first count the cost and give up everything.

verses.en: And it happened that when he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him closely.
And look, there was before him a certain man who had dropsy.
And Jesus answered and spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?”
But they kept silent. And taking hold of him, he healed him and sent him away.
And he said to them, “Which of you, if a son or an ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull him up on the Sabbath day?”

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「儿子或牛」；另有抄本是「驴或牛」，和合本跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition reads "a son or an ox"; other manuscripts read "a donkey or an ox," which the Union Version follows with 有驴或有牛 (yǒu lǘ huò yǒu niú, "has a donkey or an ox").

verses.en: And they were not able to answer back to these things.
Now he was telling a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they were choosing the places of honor, saying to them,
“When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the place of honor, lest someone more distinguished than you has been invited by him,
and the one who invited both you and him will come and say to you, ‘Give your place to this man,’ and then you will begin with shame to take the last place.

But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who has invited you comes he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher’; then you will have honor before all who recline at table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

And he was saying also to the one who had invited him, “When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not call your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you be repaid.
But when you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind;
and you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
Now one of those reclining at table with him, hearing these things, said to him, “Blessed is whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God!”
But he said to him, “A certain man was giving a great dinner, and he invited many;
and he sent his slave at the hour of the dinner to say to those who had been invited, ‘Come, for it is now ready.’
And they all alike began to make excuses. The first said to him, ‘I bought a field, and I must go out and see it; I ask you, have me excused.’
And another said, ‘I bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out; I ask you, have me excused.’
And another said, ‘I married a wife, and for that reason I cannot come.’

And the slave came and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house, becoming angry, said to his slave, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the town, and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame.’
And the slave said, ‘Master, what you commanded has been done, and still there is room.’
And the master said to the slave, ‘Go out into the roads and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled;
for I say to you that none of those men who were invited will taste my dinner.’”
Now great crowds were traveling with him, and turning he said to them,
“If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and yes, even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.

cmp.note: 原文就是「恨」。和合本译成「爱我胜过爱……」，是把这个字解释成比较的说法；《马太福音》10:37 那一句的原文才是「爱……胜过爱我」。
cmp.en: The Greek is simply "hate." The Union Version renders it 爱我胜过爱 (ài wǒ shèngguò ài, "love me more than"), explaining the word as a comparison; it is the saying in Matthew 10:37 that actually reads "loves … more than me."

verses.en: Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to complete it?
Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is not able to finish, all who see it begin to mock him,
saying, ‘This man began to build and was not able to finish.’
Or what king, going out to meet another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
So then, every one of you who does not renounce all his own possessions cannot be my disciple.
Salt, then, is good; but if even the salt has lost its taste, with what will it be seasoned?
It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; they throw it out. The one who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

chapters.title: Chapter 15 · The Lost Sheep, the Lost Coin, the Two Sons
chapters.intro: Tax collectors and sinners are all coming to hear Jesus, and the Pharisees and scribes grumble that he welcomes such people. He answers with three stories in a row: one sheep lost out of a hundred; one silver coin lost out of ten; and a father whose younger son leaves home, spends everything and comes back, at which the father holds a feast and the older son is angry. From verse 4 on it is almost all Jesus speaking.

verses.en: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.
And both the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
And he told them this parable, saying,
“What man among you, having a hundred sheep and having lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost until he finds it?
And having found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing,
and coming to his house, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.’
I say to you that in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.
Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?

cmp.note: 原文是「十个德拉克马」。德拉克马是希腊银币，价值和别处说的罗马银币差不多，约是一个工人一天的工钱。和合本写「十块钱」。
cmp.en: The Greek says "ten drachmas." The drachma was a Greek silver coin worth about the same as the Roman silver coin mentioned elsewhere, roughly a laborer’s daily wage. The Union Version writes 十块钱 (shí kuài qián, "ten pieces of money").

verses.en: And having found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I lost.’
In the same way, I say to you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.”
And he said, “A certain man had two sons.
And the younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me.’ And he divided his living between them.
And not many days later, the younger son gathered everything together and went away to a far country, and there he squandered his property, living recklessly.
And when he had spent everything, a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in need.
And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

cmp.note: 按犹太律法，猪是不洁净的动物，犹太人不吃也不养。去给人放猪，在当时的犹太听众听来，是落到了最低的地步。
cmp.en: Under Jewish law the pig is an unclean animal, which Jews neither ate nor kept. To a Jewish audience of the time, being sent to feed pigs meant having sunk as low as one could.

verses.en: And he longed to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him anything.
But coming to himself, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired men have more than enough bread, but I am perishing here with hunger!
I will get up and go to my father, and I will say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you;

cmp.note: 「天」在这里是对上帝的委婉说法：当时的犹太人常常这样避开直接说「上帝」。
cmp.en: "Heaven" here is a reverent way of saying "God"; Jews of the time often avoided naming God directly in this way.

verses.en: I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired men.”’
And he got up and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
And the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
But the father said to his slaves, ‘Quickly bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet,
and bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat and celebrate,
for this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.’ And they began to celebrate.
Now his older son was in the field; and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing,
and calling one of the servants, he asked what these things might be.
And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and sound.’
But he was angry and was not willing to go in. And his father came out and was pleading with him.

But he answered and said to his father, ‘Look, for so many years I have been slaving for you, and I never disobeyed a command of yours, yet you never gave me a young goat so that I might celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him!’

cmp.note: 大儿子不说「我弟弟」，说「你这个儿子」；下面第 32 节父亲回他的话里，说的是「你这个弟弟」。
cmp.en: The older son does not say "my brother" but "this son of yours"; in the father’s reply in verse 32 the phrase is "this brother of yours."

verses.en: And he said to him, ‘Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
But it was right to celebrate and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’”

chapters.title: Chapter 16 · The Unrighteous Manager; the Rich Man and Lazarus
chapters.intro: Jesus tells the disciples a story: a manager about to be dismissed reduces the bills of his master’s debtors, and the master praises him for his shrewdness. He goes on to speak about how to handle money and says no one can serve both God and wealth. The Pharisees, who love money, sneer at him, and he tells another story: a rich man and Lazarus, the poor man who lay at his gate, whose fortunes are reversed after death.

verses.en: And he was also saying to the disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager, and this man was accused to him of squandering his possessions.
And he called him and said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
And the manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, since my master is taking the management away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the management, they may receive me into their houses.’
And calling to him each one of his master’s debtors, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
And he said, ‘A hundred baths of oil.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’

cmp.note: 原文这里的量器叫「罢特」，下一节量麦子的叫「歌珥」，都是希伯来的容量单位：一罢特有几十升，一歌珥有几百升，所以两笔都是很大的债。和合本写成「篓」和「石」。
cmp.en: The measures here are the Hebrew "bath" (for the oil) and, in the next verse, "cor" (for the wheat): a bath is some tens of liters and a cor some hundreds, so both debts are very large. The Union Version writes 篓 (lǒu, "basket") and 石 (dàn, a Chinese grain measure).

verses.en: Then he said to another, ‘And you, how much do you owe?’ And he said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He says to him, ‘Take your bill and write eighty.’
And the master praised the unrighteous manager because he had acted shrewdly; for the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light.

cmp.note: 「主人」原文是 kyrios，这个词也可以指「主」（耶稣），所以夸奖管家的是故事里的财主还是耶稣，读法不一；多数人取前一种。这一节和下一节历来有好几种解释，本站只照字面译，不作解释。
cmp.en: The word for "master" is kyrios, which can also mean "the Lord" (Jesus), so readers differ on whether it is the rich man in the story or Jesus who praises the manager; most take it as the rich man. This verse and the next have been explained in several ways; this site translates the wording and offers no explanation.

verses.en: And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by means of the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it fails, they may receive you into the eternal tents.

cmp.note: 原文 mamōnas 是亚兰话，意思是钱财、家当。和合本在这一节和第 11 节译成「钱财」，到第 13 节照读音写成「玛门」；本站的白话都写「钱财」，英文都写 mammon。
cmp.en: The Greek mamōnas is an Aramaic word for money or property. The Union Version translates it 钱财 (qiáncái, "wealth") here and in verse 11 but writes it by sound as 玛门 (Mǎmén) in verse 13; this site’s Chinese writes 钱财 throughout and the English "mammon" throughout.

verses.en: The one who is faithful in very little is faithful also in much, and the one who is unrighteous in very little is unrighteous also in much.
If then you have not been faithful with the unrighteous mammon, who will entrust to you the true?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
No household servant can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.”
Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were hearing all these things, and they were sneering at him.
And he said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among people is an abomination before God.
The law and the prophets were until John; since then the good news of the kingdom of God is proclaimed, and everyone forces his way into it.

cmp.note: 这个动词的意思不确定：可以是「人人用力挤进去」（白话、英文和和合本的「努力要进去」都取这一种），也可以读成被动，「人人都被极力劝进去」。
cmp.en: The sense of this verb is uncertain: it may mean "everyone presses his way in" (so the plain Chinese, the English, and the Union Version’s 努力要进去, nǔlì yào jìnqù, "strives to enter"), or it may be passive, "everyone is urgently pressed to enter."

verses.en: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the law to fall.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and he who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
Now there was a certain rich man, and he used to dress in purple and fine linen, feasting splendidly every day.
And a certain poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gate, covered with sores,
and longing to be fed with what fell from the rich man’s table; even the dogs came and licked his sores.
And it happened that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom; and the rich man also died and was buried.

cmp.note: 「在某人怀里」原是说宴席上紧挨着主人斜靠的位子。「亚伯拉罕的怀里」是当时犹太人对义人死后安息之处的一种说法。
cmp.en: "In someone’s bosom" originally describes the place next to the host when reclining at a banquet. "Abraham’s bosom" was one way Jews of the time spoke of where the righteous rest after death.

verses.en: And in Hades, lifting up his eyes, being in torment, he sees Abraham from afar and Lazarus in his bosom.
And he called out and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in agony in this flame.’

cmp.note: 原文是「父亲亚伯拉罕」。犹太人称亚伯拉罕为「我们的父」，意思是始祖；白话写「祖宗」，和合本写「我祖」。下面亚伯拉罕回答时也叫他「孩子」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "Father Abraham." Jews called Abraham "our father," meaning their first ancestor; the plain Chinese writes 祖宗 (zǔzōng, "forefather") and the Union Version 我祖 (wǒ zǔ, "my ancestor"). Abraham in turn answers him as "child."

verses.en: But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and Lazarus likewise the bad things; but now he is comforted here, and you are in agony.
And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those who want to cross over from here to you cannot, nor may they cross from there to us.’
And he said, ‘Then I ask you, father, to send him to my father’s house,
for I have five brothers, so that he may warn them, lest they also come to this place of torment.’
But Abraham says, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.’
But he said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
But he said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.’”

chapters.title: Chapter 17 · Forgiveness and Faith; Ten Men Healed; the Day of the Son of Man
chapters.intro: Jesus teaches the disciples not to make others stumble, to forgive a brother who repents, and not to claim credit for doing their duty. On the way to Jerusalem he heals ten men with a skin disease, and only one, a Samaritan, comes back to thank him. Asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God will come, he says it is in their midst, and he tells the disciples that the day the Son of Man is revealed will come suddenly.

verses.en: And he said to his disciples, “It is impossible that the causes of stumbling should not come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him;
and if he sins against you seven times in the day and seven times turns back to you, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
And the apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”

cmp.note: 这卷书的叙述里常常直接把耶稣叫做「主」，这一节和下一节都是。
cmp.en: The narrator of this Gospel often refers to Jesus simply as "the Lord," as in this verse and the next.

verses.en: And the Lord said, “If you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
But which of you, having a slave plowing or keeping sheep, will say to him when he has come in from the field, ‘Come at once and recline at table’?
Will he not rather say to him, ‘Prepare something for me to eat, and gird yourself and serve me until I have eaten and drunk, and after that you shall eat and drink’?
Does he thank the slave because he did what was commanded?
So you also, when you have done all that was commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy slaves; we have done what we ought to have done.’”
And it happened, as he was going to Jerusalem, that he was passing through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
And as he was entering a certain village, ten men with a skin disease met him, who stood at a distance,
and they raised their voice, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

cmp.note: 这里的「老师」原文是 epistata，只有路加福音用这个称呼，本义是「在上头管事的人」；别处称耶稣「老师」多半用 didaskale。白话都写「老师」，和合本都写「夫子」，英文这里写 Master。
cmp.en: The word for "Master" here is epistata, a form of address found only in Luke, originally "one set over others"; elsewhere Jesus is usually addressed as didaskale, "teacher." The plain Chinese writes 老师 (lǎoshī, "teacher") for both and the Union Version 夫子 (fūzǐ, "master") for both.

verses.en: And seeing them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” And it happened that as they went, they were made clean.

cmp.note: 按犹太律法（旧约《利未记》13–14 章），得这种病的人算「不洁净」，要离开人群住；病好了，要由祭司检查、宣布洁净，才能回去。
cmp.en: Under Jewish law (Leviticus 13–14) a person with this disease was "unclean" and had to live apart; once well, he had to be examined and declared clean by a priest before he could return.

verses.en: Now one of them, seeing that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice,
and he fell on his face at his feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
And Jesus answered and said, “Were not the ten made clean? But the nine, where are they?
Was no one found returning to give glory to God except this foreigner?”
And he said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has saved you.”
Now being asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God is coming, he answered them and said, “The kingdom of God does not come with observation,
nor will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘There!’ For look, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”

cmp.note: 这两个词可以读成「在你们中间」，也可以读成「在你们里面」。白话和英文取前一种，和合本取后一种，写「在你们心里」。
cmp.en: The two words can be read "in your midst" or "within you." The plain Chinese and the English take the first; the Union Version takes the second and writes 在你们心里 (zài nǐmen xīn lǐ, "in your hearts").

verses.en: And he said to the disciples, “Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
And they will say to you, ‘Look, there!’ ‘Look, here!’ Do not go out and do not pursue.
For just as the lightning, when it flashes, shines from one part under heaven to the other part under heaven, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
And just as it happened in the days of Noah, so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man:
they were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
Likewise, just as it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building;
but on the day Lot went out from Sodom, fire and sulfur rained from heaven and destroyed them all.
It will be the same on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever is on the housetop, with his goods in the house, let him not come down to take them, and likewise let the one in the field not turn back.
Remember Lot’s wife.

cmp.note: 旧约《创世记》19 章说，罗得一家逃离所多玛的时候，他的妻子回头看了一眼，就变成了一根盐柱。
cmp.en: Genesis 19 tells that as Lot’s family fled Sodom, his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.

verses.en: Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will keep it alive.
I say to you, on that night there will be two in one bed; the one will be taken and the other will be left.
There will be two women grinding together; the one will be taken and the other will be left.”
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本在这里有一句话，意思是：两个人在田里，一个要被带走，一个要被留下。最早的几份抄本没有这一句，一般认为是抄写的人照《马太福音》24:40 补进来的，所以底本不收。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have a sentence here meaning: two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left. The earliest manuscripts lack it, and it is generally thought that copyists added it from Matthew 24:40, so the edition leaves it out.

verses.en: And answering they say to him, “Where, Lord?” And he said to them, “Where the body is, there the eagles also will be gathered.”

cmp.note: 「鹰」也可以指吃腐肉的秃鹫。这句话像一句俗语，经文没有解释它指什么。
cmp.en: The word for "eagles" can also mean carrion-eating vultures. The saying sounds like a proverb, and the text does not explain what it refers to.

chapters.title: Chapter 18 · The Widow and the Judge; the Pharisee and the Tax Collector; the Rich Ruler
chapters.intro: Jesus tells two stories: a widow who keeps going to an unrighteous judge until she gets justice, and a Pharisee and a tax collector praying in the temple, of whom it is the tax collector who goes home justified. He welcomes little children, tells a rich ruler to sell everything and follow him, and once more foretells that he will be killed and rise on the third day. Near Jericho he gives a blind man his sight.

verses.en: And he was telling them a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray and not lose heart,
saying, “In a certain city there was a judge who did not fear God and did not respect man.
And there was a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
And for a time he was not willing; but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I do not fear God nor respect man,
yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice, so that she will not wear me out by her continual coming.’”

cmp.note: 这个动词的本义是「打得人眼眶发青」，这里一般理解为引申的说法：把人烦得受不了。和合本译「缠磨」。
cmp.en: The verb literally means "to give someone a black eye"; here it is generally taken figuratively, "to wear someone down." The Union Version has 缠磨 (chánmó, "to pester").

verses.en: And the Lord said, “Hear what the unrighteous judge says.
And will not God bring about justice for his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night, and is he slow to act for them?

cmp.note: 末了这半句意思不确定：可以读成问句「他难道会迟迟不管他们吗」（白话和英文这样译），也可以读成「虽然他对他们一直忍耐着」（和合本「纵然为他们忍了多时」）。
cmp.en: The last clause is uncertain: it can be read as a question, "and is he slow to act for them?" (so the plain Chinese and the English), or as "even though he is patient over them" (so the Union Version: 纵然为他们忍了多时, zòngrán wèi tāmen rěn le duō shí, "though he has long borne with them").

verses.en: I say to you that he will bring about justice for them quickly. Yet when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
And he also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and looked down on everyone else:
“Two men went up to the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee, standing, was praying these things to himself: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of men, swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all that I get.’
But the tax collector, standing far off, was not willing even to lift up his eyes to heaven, but was beating his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, the sinner!’
I say to you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
Now they were bringing even their infants to him so that he might touch them; but when the disciples saw it, they were rebuking them.
But Jesus called them to him, saying, “Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will certainly not enter it.”
And a certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
And Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God.
You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”

cmp.note: 这几条出自「十诫」，见旧约《出埃及记》20:12–16、《申命记》5:16–20。
cmp.en: These are from the Ten Commandments: Exodus 20:12–16 and Deuteronomy 5:16–20.

verses.en: And he said, “All these I have kept from my youth.”
And hearing this, Jesus said to him, “One thing you still lack: sell all that you have and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow me.”
But hearing these things, he became very sad, for he was extremely rich.
And looking at him, Jesus said, “How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
And those who heard said, “Then who can be saved?”
But he said, “What is impossible with men is possible with God.”
And Peter said, “Look, we have left what was ours and followed you.”
And he said to them, “Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the age to come eternal life.”
And taking the twelve aside, he said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be accomplished.
For he will be handed over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spat upon,
and having flogged him they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.”
And they understood none of these things, and this saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was being said.
Now it happened, as he was drawing near to Jericho, that a certain blind man was sitting beside the road begging.
And hearing a crowd going through, he asked what this might be.
And they told him, “Jesus the Nazorean is passing by.”
And he cried out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
And those who were going ahead were rebuking him so that he would be silent; but he was crying out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
And Jesus stopped and ordered him to be brought to him; and when he came near, he asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?” And he said, “Lord, let me see again.”
And Jesus said to him, “See again; your faith has saved you.”
And at once he saw again, and he was following him, glorifying God. And all the people, seeing it, gave praise to God.

chapters.title: Chapter 19 · Zacchaeus; the Ten Minas; Entering Jerusalem
chapters.intro: Passing through Jericho, Jesus stays at the house of Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who promises to give half of what he owns to the poor. He tells a story about a nobleman who entrusts money to ten slaves to trade with. Then he rides a colt toward Jerusalem; the disciples shout for joy, but he weeps over the city. Entering the temple, he drives out those who are selling and teaches there every day.

verses.en: And having entered, he was passing through Jericho.
And look, there was a man called by the name Zacchaeus, and he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

cmp.note: 税吏是替罗马人向本地人收税的人，常常多收，所以被同胞看不起；税吏长是管着一批税吏的头目。
cmp.en: Tax collectors gathered taxes from the local people on behalf of Rome and often overcharged, so their own people despised them; a chief tax collector was in charge of a number of them.

verses.en: And he was seeking to see who Jesus was, and he could not because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
And running on ahead, he climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was about to pass that way.

cmp.note: 原文指的是一种枝干低、容易爬的无花果类的树，和第 17 章第 6 节的「桑树」（sykaminos）不是同一个词；和合本两处都译「桑树」，白话跟着写。
cmp.en: The Greek names a low-branched, easily climbed tree of the fig family; it is not the same word as the "mulberry tree" (sykaminos) of 17:6. The Union Version writes 桑树 (sāngshù, "mulberry tree") in both places, and the plain Chinese follows it.

verses.en: And when he came to the place, Jesus looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
And he hurried and came down and received him joyfully.
And seeing it, they were all grumbling, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”
But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Look, half of my possessions, Lord, I give to the poor, and if I have extorted anything from anyone, I pay it back fourfold.”
And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham;
for the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
Now as they were listening to these things, he went on to tell a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they supposed that the kingdom of God was about to appear at once.
He said therefore, “A certain man of noble birth went to a far country to receive a kingdom for himself and to return.
And calling ten of his slaves, he gave them ten minas and said to them, ‘Do business until I come.’

cmp.note: 原文的钱数单位叫「弥拿」，一弥拿合一百个银币，约是一个工人一百天的工钱。十个仆人共十弥拿，就是每人一弥拿。和合本写「锭」，白话跟着写；英文照音写 mina。
cmp.en: The unit is the mina, worth a hundred silver coins, about a hundred days’ wages for a laborer. Ten minas among ten slaves is one each. The Union Version writes 锭 (dìng, "ingot"), which the plain Chinese follows; the English keeps "mina."

verses.en: But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’

And it happened that when he returned, having received the kingdom, he ordered these slaves to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he might know what they had gained by doing business.
And the first came, saying, ‘Master, your mina has made ten minas more.’
And he said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because you have been faithful in a very little, have authority over ten cities.’
And the second came, saying, ‘Your mina, master, has made five minas.’
And he said to this one also, ‘And you, be over five cities.’
And the other came, saying, ‘Master, look, here is your mina, which I kept laid away in a cloth;
for I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man; you take up what you did not lay down and reap what you did not sow.’
He says to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I will judge you, wicked slave! You knew that I am a severe man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?
Then why did you not put my money in the bank, and at my coming I would have collected it with interest?’
And he said to those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has the ten minas.’
And they said to him, ‘Master, he has ten minas!’
‘I say to you that to everyone who has, more will be given, but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slaughter them before me.’”
And having said these things, he was going on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
And it happened, when he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mountain called Olivet, that he sent two of the disciples,
saying, “Go into the village opposite, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever yet sat; untie it and bring it.
And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ you shall say this: ‘The Lord has need of it.’”
And those who were sent went away and found it just as he had told them.
And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”

cmp.note: 驴驹的「主人们」和下一节的「主」在原文是同一个词（kyrios），只是一个复数、一个单数。
cmp.en: The "owners" of the colt and "the Lord" in the next verse are the same Greek word (kyrios), the one plural and the other singular.

verses.en: And they said, “The Lord has need of it.”
And they brought it to Jesus, and throwing their garments on the colt, they set Jesus on it.
And as he was going along, they were spreading their garments on the road.

And as he was now drawing near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen,
saying, “Blessed is the one who comes, the king, in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”

cmp.note: 前半句出自旧约《诗篇》118:26（「奉主的名来的，是应当称颂的」），这里多了一个「王」字。
cmp.en: The first half comes from Psalm 118:26 ("Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord"), with the word "king" added here.

verses.en: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.”
And he answered and said, “I say to you, if these are silent, the stones will cry out.”
And when he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it,
saying, “If you had known on this day, even you, the things that make for peace—but now they have been hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when your enemies will throw up a rampart against you and surround you and hem you in on every side,
and they will dash you to the ground, you and your children within you, and they will not leave stone upon stone in you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.”
And entering the temple, he began to drive out those who were selling,
saying to them, “It is written, ‘And my house shall be a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers.”

cmp.note: 前一句引旧约《以赛亚书》56:7，「强盗窝」出自《耶利米书》7:11。和合本把后一个词译成「贼窝」。
cmp.en: The first phrase quotes Isaiah 56:7; "den of robbers" comes from Jeremiah 7:11. The Union Version renders the latter 贼窝 (zéiwō, "den of thieves").

verses.en: And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy him, and so were the leading men of the people,
and they could not find what they might do, for all the people were hanging on his words.

chapters.title: Chapter 20 · Questions in the Temple: Authority, Taxes, Resurrection
chapters.intro: Jesus is teaching in the temple. The chief priests, scribes and elders demand to know by what authority he acts, and he asks them in return where John’s baptism came from. He tells a parable of tenants who kill the owner’s son. Spies ask whether taxes should be paid to Caesar, and Sadducees ask whose wife a woman will be in the resurrection; he answers both. Finally he asks how the Christ can be David’s son, and warns his disciples against the scribes.

verses.en: And it happened on one of the days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, that the chief priests and the scribes came up with the elders,
and they spoke, saying to him, “Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who it is who gave you this authority.”
And answering, he said to them, “I also will ask you a question, and you tell me:
The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from men?”
And they reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
And they answered that they did not know where it was from.
And Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
And he began to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard and let it out to tenants and went abroad for a long time.
And at the season he sent a slave to the tenants, so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard; but the tenants beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And he went on to send another slave; but that one also they beat and dishonored and sent away empty-handed.
And he went on to send a third; and this one also they wounded and threw out.
And the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’
But when the tenants saw him, they reasoned with one another, saying, ‘This is the heir; let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.’
And throwing him out of the vineyard, they killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy these tenants and give the vineyard to others.” And when they heard it they said, “May it never be!”
But he looked at them and said, “What then is this that is written: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner’?

cmp.note: 这一句引自旧约《诗篇》118:22。「房角的头」指墙角上最要紧的那块石头。
cmp.en: The line is quoted from Psalm 118:22. "Head of the corner" means the most important stone at the corner of a wall.

verses.en: Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces; and on whomever it falls, it will crush him.”
And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on him in that very hour, and they feared the people; for they knew that he had told this parable against them.
And watching him closely, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch him in something he said, so as to hand him over to the rule and the authority of the governor.
And they asked him, saying, “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly and show no partiality, but teach the way of God in truth.
Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?”
But perceiving their craftiness, he said to them,
“Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?” And answering, they said, “Caesar’s.”
And he said to them, “Then give back to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
And they were not able to catch him in his word before the people, and marveling at his answer they fell silent.
And there came some of the Sadducees, those who say that there is no resurrection, and they asked him,
saying, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.

cmp.note: 这条规定见旧约《申命记》25:5–6：哥哥死了没有儿子，弟弟要娶嫂子，生的头一个儿子算在哥哥名下。
cmp.en: The rule is in Deuteronomy 25:5–6: if a man dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow, and the first son born counts as the dead man’s.

verses.en: Now there were seven brothers; and the first took a wife and died childless;
and the second
and the third took her, and likewise all seven left no children and died.
Afterward the woman also died.
The woman, then, in the resurrection, whose wife does she become? For the seven had her as wife.”
And Jesus said to them, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage,
but those who are counted worthy to attain to that age and to the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage;
for they cannot die anymore, for they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed in the passage about the bush, where he calls the Lord the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.

cmp.note: 「荆棘那一段」指旧约《出埃及记》第 3 章：上帝在烧着却没有烧毁的荆棘里向摩西说话。当时的经书没有章节号，就用故事里的东西来称呼一段。
cmp.en: "The passage about the bush" is Exodus 3, where God speaks to Moses from a bush that burns without being consumed. Scripture then had no chapter numbers, so a passage was named after something in it.

verses.en: Now he is not God of the dead but of the living, for all live to him.”
And some of the scribes answered and said, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”
For they no longer dared to ask him anything.
But he said to them, “How do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
For David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand,

cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》110:1。前一个「主」指上帝，后一个「我的主」，耶稣在这里说的是基督。
cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 110:1. The first "Lord" is God; the second, "my Lord," is the one Jesus here takes to be the Christ.

verses.en: until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.’
David then calls him Lord; and how is he his son?”
And while all the people were listening, he said to the disciples,
“Beware of the scribes, who want to walk about in long robes and love greetings in the marketplaces and the first seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at dinners,
who devour widows’ houses and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”

chapters.title: Chapter 21 · The Widow’s Two Coins; the Temple’s Fall Foretold
chapters.intro: Jesus praises a poor widow who gives two small coins. When some admire the temple, he says that not one stone of it will be left on another. Then comes a long speech: there will be wars and persecution, Jerusalem will be surrounded by armies and trampled by the nations, and afterward the Son of Man will come in a cloud; so stay awake at all times. From verse 8 to verse 36 it is almost all Jesus speaking.

verses.en: And looking up, he saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
And he saw a certain poor widow putting in two lepta there,

cmp.note: 原文 lepton 是当时最小的铜钱，两个加起来也买不了什么。和合本译「小钱」。
cmp.en: A lepton was the smallest copper coin of the time; two of them bought next to nothing. The Union Version has 小钱 (xiǎo qián, "small coins").

verses.en: and he said, “Truly I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them;
for all these put in their gifts out of their abundance, but she out of her want has put in all the living that she had.”
And as some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones and offerings, he said,
“These things that you are looking at, days will come in which there will not be left a stone upon a stone that will not be thrown down.”
And they asked him, saying, “Teacher, when then will these things be, and what will be the sign when these things are about to happen?”
And he said, “See that you are not led astray; for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has come near.’ Do not go after them.
And when you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end is not at once.”
Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom,
and there will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and plagues, and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to the synagogues and prisons, being led away before kings and governors for the sake of my name.
It will turn out for you as a testimony.
Settle it therefore in your hearts not to practice beforehand how to make your defense,
for I will give you a mouth and wisdom that all your opponents will not be able to withstand or contradict.
And you will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death,
and you will be hated by all because of my name.
And not a hair of your head will perish.
By your endurance gain your lives.
But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near.
Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those inside the city get out, and let those in the country not enter it,
for these are days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.
Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people,
and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations in perplexity at the roaring of the sea and the waves,
people fainting from fear and expectation of what is coming on the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
Now when these things begin to happen, stand up straight and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”
And he told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees;
when they are already putting out leaves, you see it and know for yourselves that the summer is already near.
So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly I say to you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
But watch yourselves, so that your hearts are not weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the cares of this life, and that day come upon you suddenly
like a trap; for it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
But stay awake at every moment, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”
And during the days he was teaching in the temple, but at night he went out and lodged on the mount called Olivet.
And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.

chapters.title: Chapter 22 · The Last Supper; Arrest on the Mount of Olives; Peter’s Denial
chapters.intro: The Passover is near, and Judas agrees to hand Jesus over to the chief priests. Jesus eats the Passover meal with the apostles, speaks of the bread and the cup as his body and blood, tells them the greatest among them must be like one who serves, and foretells that Peter will deny him three times. He prays on the Mount of Olives and is then arrested; in the high priest’s courtyard Peter denies him three times. At daybreak he is brought before the council.

verses.en: Now the feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was drawing near.
And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might do away with him, for they feared the people.
And Satan entered into Judas, the one called Iscariot, who was of the number of the twelve;
and he went off and discussed with the chief priests and officers how he might hand him over to them.
And they were glad, and agreed to give him money.
And he consented, and was seeking an opportunity to hand him over to them apart from the crowd.
Then came the day of Unleavened Bread, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
And he sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat it.”
And they said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare it?”
And he said to them, “Look, when you have entered the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him into the house that he enters,
and you shall say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’
And that man will show you a large upper room, furnished; prepare there.”
And they went off and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when the hour came, he reclined at table, and the apostles with him.
And he said to them, “With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer;

cmp.note: 字面是「我以盼望盼望了」，同一个词说两遍，是从希伯来话来的加重说法，意思是「非常盼望」。英文照字面保留了这个重复。
cmp.en: Literally "with desire I desired": saying the word twice is an emphatic turn carried over from Hebrew, meaning "I have greatly desired." The English keeps the doubling; the Chinese writes 非常盼望 (fēicháng pànwàng, "very much hoped").

verses.en: for I say to you that I will certainly not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
And taking a cup, having given thanks, he said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves;
for I say to you, I will certainly not drink from now on of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”
And taking bread, having given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body [which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”

cmp.note: 从「是为你们舍的」起，到下一节末尾，底本用方括号括着：绝大多数抄本有这一段，但有少数古抄本没有，所以编者标了记号。和合本有这一段。照这段经文，晚餐上先后有两次杯（第 17 节、第 20 节）。
cmp.en: From "which is given for you" to the end of the next verse the edition prints the words in square brackets: the great majority of manuscripts have them, but a few ancient ones do not, so the editors marked them. The Union Version includes them. With these words the meal has two cups (verses 17 and 20).

verses.en: And the cup likewise after they had eaten, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.]
But look, the hand of the one who is handing me over is with me on the table.
For the Son of Man goes as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is handed over!”
And they began to question among themselves which of them it could be who was going to do this.
And there also arose a dispute among them as to which of them was considered to be greatest.
