And he said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors.

cmp.note: 「恩主」（euergetēs）是当时希腊化世界里君王和大人物常用的尊号，意思是「施恩的人」。
cmp.en: "Benefactor" (euergetēs) was a title of honor commonly given to kings and great men in the Greek-speaking world of the time.

verses.en: But not so with you; rather let the greatest among you become as the youngest, and the one who leads as the one who serves.
For who is greater, the one who reclines at table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as the one who serves.
You are those who have stayed with me in my trials;
and I assign to you, as my Father assigned to me, a kingdom,
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Simon, Simon, look, Satan demanded to have you all, to sift you like wheat;
but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”

cmp.note: 上一节的「你们」是复数，指所有的门徒；这一节的「你」是单数，专指西门（就是彼得）。
cmp.en: The "you" of the previous verse is plural, all the disciples; the "you" of this verse is singular, Simon (that is, Peter) alone.

verses.en: But he said to him, “Lord, with you I am ready to go both to prison and to death.”
But he said, “I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you have three times denied that you know me.”
And he said to them, “When I sent you out without purse and bag and sandals, did you lack anything?” And they said, “Nothing.”
And he said to them, “But now, let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag; and let the one who has no sword sell his cloak and buy one.
For I say to you that this which is written must be fulfilled in me: ‘And he was counted with the lawless.’ For what concerns me is coming to its end.”

cmp.note: 这一句引自旧约《以赛亚书》53:12，那一章讲一位替别人受苦的「仆人」。
cmp.en: The line is quoted from Isaiah 53:12, a chapter about a "servant" who suffers for others.

verses.en: And they said, “Lord, look, here are two swords.” And he said to them, “It is enough.”
And going out, he went as was his custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed him.
And when he came to the place, he said to them, “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, and kneeling down he was praying,
saying, “Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me; yet not my will but yours be done.”
And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.

cmp.note: 第 43、44 两节，本站的底本和多数抄本都有，和合本也有；但有好几份很早的抄本没有这两节。它们是不是原来就有，学者看法不一。
cmp.en: Verses 43 and 44 are in this site’s edition, in most manuscripts and in the Union Version, but several very early manuscripts lack them. Scholars disagree on whether they were there from the start.

verses.en: And being in agony he was praying more earnestly; and his sweat became like drops of blood falling down upon the ground.

cmp.note: 原文说汗「像」血滴一样落下，是打比方。这一节和上一节一样，有好几份很早的抄本没有（见上一节的注）。
cmp.en: The Greek says the sweat fell "like" drops of blood, a comparison. Like the previous verse, this one is missing from several very early manuscripts (see the note there).

verses.en: And rising from prayer, he came to the disciples and found them sleeping from grief,
and he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, that you may not enter into temptation.”
While he was still speaking, look, a crowd, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going before them; and he drew near to Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus said to him, “Judas, do you hand over the Son of Man with a kiss?”
And those around him, seeing what was about to happen, said, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”
And a certain one of them struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus answered and said, “No more of this!” And touching the ear, he healed him.

cmp.note: 原文只有三个词，字面是「容许，到这里」。本站读成对门徒说的「到此为止，不要再动手」；和合本读成「到了这个地步，由他们吧」。两种读法都有人主张。
cmp.en: The Greek is three words, literally "allow, as far as this." This site takes it as said to the disciples: "No more of this." The Union Version takes it as 到了这个地步、由他们罢 (dào le zhège dìbù, yóu tāmen ba, "it has come to this; let them be"). Both readings have their supporters.

verses.en: And Jesus said to those who had come out against him, chief priests and officers of the temple and elders, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”
And having seized him, they led him away and brought him into the house of the high priest; and Peter was following at a distance.
And when they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them.
And a certain servant girl, seeing him sitting in the firelight and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him.”
But he denied it, saying, “I do not know him, woman.”
And after a little while another saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
And when about one hour had passed, a certain other man kept insisting, saying, “In truth this man also was with him, for he too is a Galilean.”
But Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” And at once, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
And the Lord turned and looked at Peter; and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said to him, “Before a rooster crows today, you will deny me three times.”
And going outside, he wept bitterly.
And the men who were holding him were mocking him as they beat him,
and having blindfolded him they were asking him, saying, “Prophesy! Who is it that struck you?”
And they were saying many other things against him, reviling him.
And when day came, the council of elders of the people gathered, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him away to their council,
saying, “If you are the Christ, tell us.” But he said to them, “If I tell you, you will certainly not believe;
and if I ask, you will certainly not answer.
But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
And they all said, “Are you then the Son of God?” And he said to them, “You say that I am.”

cmp.note: 字面是「你们说我是」。这句话没有直接说「是」，也没有否认；和合本译成「你们所说的是」，读成了承认。
cmp.en: Literally "You say that I am." The reply neither says a plain yes nor denies it; the Union Version’s 你们所说的是 (nǐmen suǒ shuō de shì, "what you say is so") reads it as an admission.

verses.en: And they said, “What further need do we have of testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from his own mouth.”

chapters.title: Chapter 23 · Before Pilate and Herod; the Crucifixion and Burial
chapters.intro: The council brings Jesus to the Roman governor Pilate and accuses him. Pilate finds no guilt and sends him to Herod, who mocks him and sends him back. Three times Pilate says he will release him, but the crowd demands Barabbas and calls for Jesus to be crucified. Jesus is crucified at the place called The Skull with a criminal on either side; from noon darkness covers the land, and he breathes his last. Joseph lays him in a tomb.

verses.en: And the whole company of them rose up and led him before Pilate.
And they began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man misleading our nation and forbidding to pay taxes to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king.”
And Pilate asked him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” And answering him he said, “You say so.”
And Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no guilt in this man.”
But they kept insisting, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place.”
And when Pilate heard it, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
And having learned that he was from Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him up to Herod, who was himself also in Jerusalem in those days.
And when Herod saw Jesus he was very glad, for he had long wanted to see him because of what he had heard about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.
And he questioned him at some length, but he answered him nothing.
And the chief priests and the scribes stood by, vehemently accusing him.
And Herod with his soldiers also treated him with contempt and mocked him, and putting splendid clothing on him he sent him back to Pilate.
And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day, for before this they had been at enmity with each other.
And Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
said to them, “You brought this man to me as one who was misleading the people, and look, having examined him before you, I found in this man no guilt in the things of which you accuse him.
Neither did Herod, for he sent him back to us; and look, nothing deserving death has been done by him.
I will therefore discipline him and release him.”
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本在这里有一句话，意思是：每逢这个节期，总督必须给他们释放一个囚犯。最早的几份抄本没有这一节，一般认为是抄写的人照《马可福音》15:6、《马太福音》27:15 补进来的，所以底本不收。节号照旧留着，后面各节的编号才不会变。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have a sentence here meaning that at each festival the governor was obliged to release one prisoner to them. The earliest manuscripts lack the verse, and it is generally thought that copyists supplied it from Mark 15:6 and Matthew 27:15, so the edition leaves it out. The verse number is kept so that the numbering of the following verses does not change.

verses.en: But they cried out all together, saying, “Away with this man, and release to us Barabbas!”
He was one who had been thrown into prison for a certain insurrection that had taken place in the city and for murder.
And Pilate addressed them again, wanting to release Jesus;
but they kept shouting, saying, “Crucify, crucify him!”
And he said to them a third time, “Why, what evil has this man done? I found in him no guilt deserving death; I will therefore discipline him and release him.”
But they pressed on with loud voices, asking that he be crucified, and their voices prevailed.
And Pilate gave sentence that their demand be carried out.
And he released the one who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, whom they were asking for, but Jesus he handed over to their will.
And as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, and laid the cross on him to carry it behind Jesus.
And there was following him a great multitude of the people, and of women who were beating their breasts and lamenting him.
But turning to them Jesus said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children,
for look, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nurse!’
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall on us,’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us.’

cmp.note: 这两句话出自旧约《何西阿书》10:8，那里讲的是灾祸临头时人们宁愿被山压住。
cmp.en: These two cries come from Hosea 10:8, where people facing disaster would rather be buried by the hills.

verses.en: For if they do these things when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
And two others also, criminals, were being led away to be put to death with him.
And when they came to the place that is called The Skull, there they crucified him, and the criminals, one on the right and one on the left.
And Jesus was saying, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And dividing his garments, they cast lots.

cmp.note: 「父啊，赦免他们……」这一句，本站的底本和多数抄本都有，和合本也有；但有好几份很早的抄本没有。它是不是原来就有，学者看法不一。
cmp.en: The saying "Father, forgive them…" is in this site’s edition, in most manuscripts and in the Union Version, but several very early manuscripts lack it. Scholars disagree on whether it was there from the start.

verses.en: And the people stood watching. And the rulers also were sneering, saying, “He saved others; let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”
And the soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him sour wine
and saying, “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself.”
And there was also an inscription over him: “This is the King of the Jews.”
And one of the criminals who were hanged was reviling him, saying, “Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us.”
But the other answered and, rebuking him, said, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
And we indeed justly, for we are receiving what our deeds deserve; but this man has done nothing wrong.”
And he was saying, “Jesus, remember me when you come in your kingdom.”

cmp.w: hotan elthēis en tēi basileiāi sou
cmp.note: 本站的底本是「你在你的国里来到的时候」（就是带着王权来的时候）；另有一些重要的抄本是「你进入你的国的时候」，只差一个介词。和合本译「你得国降临的时候」。
cmp.en: This site’s edition reads "when you come in your kingdom" (that is, come as king); other important manuscripts read "when you come into your kingdom," a difference of one preposition. The Union Version has 你得国降临的时候 (nǐ dé guó jiànglín de shíhou, "when you come having received the kingdom").

verses.en: And he said to him, “Truly I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
And it was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
the sun having failed; and the curtain of the temple was torn in the middle.
And calling out with a loud voice, Jesus said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.” And having said this, he breathed his last.

cmp.w: eis cheiras sou paratithemai to pneuma mou
cmp.note: 这句话出自旧约《诗篇》31:5，耶稣在前面加了一声「父啊」。
cmp.en: The words come from Psalm 31:5; Jesus adds "Father" in front.

verses.en: Now when the centurion saw what had happened, he was glorifying God, saying, “Certainly this man was righteous.”
And all the crowds who had gathered for this spectacle, when they saw what had happened, returned beating their breasts.
And all those who knew him stood at a distance, and the women who had followed him from Galilee, seeing these things.
And look, a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man—
this man had not consented to their plan and action—from Arimathea, a town of the Jews, who was waiting for the kingdom of God,
this man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus,
and taking it down he wrapped it in a linen cloth and laid him in a tomb cut in the rock, where no one had ever yet been laid.
And it was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was beginning.
And the women who had come with him from Galilee followed after and saw the tomb and how his body was laid;
and returning, they prepared spices and ointments. And on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment,

chapters.title: Chapter 24 · The Empty Tomb; the Road to Emmaus; the Ascension
chapters.intro: Early on Sunday the women come to the tomb and find the stone rolled away and the body gone; two men in dazzling clothes tell them Jesus has been raised. That same day two of his followers meet him on the road to Emmaus without recognizing him, until he breaks the bread. Jesus then appears to the disciples gathered in Jerusalem, eats a piece of fish, explains the scriptures to them, and near Bethany is carried up into heaven.

verses.en: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices that they had prepared.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
but when they went in they did not find the body.
And it happened, while they were perplexed about this, that look, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.
And as they became frightened and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, “Why do you seek the living one among the dead?
He is not here, but has been raised. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee,
saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men and be crucified and on the third day rise.”
And they remembered his words,
and returning from the tomb they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
Now they were Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the mother of James and the rest of the women with them; they were telling these things to the apostles.
And these words appeared to them as nonsense, and they did not believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb; and stooping and looking in, he sees the linen cloths alone; and he went away to his home, marveling at what had happened.
And look, two of them on that same day were going to a village named Emmaus, sixty stadia from Jerusalem,
and they were talking with each other about all these things that had happened.
And it happened, while they were talking and discussing, that Jesus himself drew near and was going with them,
but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
And he said to them, “What are these words that you are exchanging with each other as you walk?” And they stood still, looking sad.
And one of them, named Cleopas, answered and said to him, “Are you the only one staying in Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?”
And he said to them, “What things?” And they said to him, “The things about Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to be condemned to death, and crucified him.
But we were hoping that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel. Yes, and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
Moreover, some women of our company amazed us: having been at the tomb early in the morning
and not having found his body, they came saying that they had even seen a vision of angels, who say that he is alive.
And some of those with us went off to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see.”
And he said to them, “O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into his glory?”
And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
And they drew near to the village where they were going, and he acted as though he were going farther.
And they urged him strongly, saying, “Stay with us, for it is toward evening and the day is already far spent.” And he went in to stay with them.
And it happened, when he had reclined at table with them, that he took the bread and blessed it, and having broken it he was giving it to them.
And their eyes were opened and they recognized him; and he vanished from their sight.
And they said to each other, “Was not our heart burning within us as he was speaking to us on the road, as he was opening the scriptures to us?”
And rising up that very hour they returned to Jerusalem, and they found the eleven and those with them gathered together,
saying, “The Lord has really been raised and has appeared to Simon!”
And they themselves were telling what had happened on the road and how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
And as they were saying these things, he himself stood in their midst.
But they were startled and became frightened, and thought they were seeing a spirit.
And he said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your heart?
See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.”
[And having said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.]

cmp.note: 这一整节，底本放在方括号里：绝大多数抄本有，但有少数古抄本没有，所以编者标了记号。和合本有。
cmp.en: This whole verse: The edition prints it in square brackets: the great majority of manuscripts have them, but a few ancient ones do not, so the editors marked them. The Union Version includes them.

verses.en: And while they still did not believe for joy and were marveling, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
And they gave him a piece of broiled fish;
and he took it and ate before them.
And he said to them, “These are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms must be fulfilled.”

cmp.w: en tōi nomōi Mōÿseōs kai prophētais kai psalmois
cmp.note: 「摩西的律法、先知的书、诗篇」是犹太人经书的三大部分，合起来就是指整部旧约。
cmp.en: "The law of Moses, the prophets and the psalms" are the three main divisions of the Jewish scriptures; together they mean the whole Old Testament.

verses.en: Then he opened their mind to understand the scriptures,
and he said to them, “Thus it is written, that the Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all the nations—beginning from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
And look, I am sending the promise of my Father upon you; but you, stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.”
And he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands he blessed them.
And it happened, while he was blessing them, that he parted from them [and was being carried up into heaven].

cmp.note: 「被带到天上去了」：底本把这几个字放在方括号里：绝大多数抄本有，但有少数古抄本没有，所以编者标了记号。和合本有。
cmp.en: "And was being carried up into heaven": The edition prints these words in square brackets: the great majority of manuscripts have them, but a few ancient ones do not, so the editors marked them. The Union Version includes them.

verses.en: And they, [having worshiped him,] returned to Jerusalem with great joy,

cmp.note: 「拜了他」：底本把这几个字放在方括号里：绝大多数抄本有，但有少数古抄本没有，所以编者标了记号。和合本有。
cmp.en: "Having worshiped him": The edition prints these words in square brackets: the great majority of manuscripts have them, but a few ancient ones do not, so the editors marked them. The Union Version includes them.

verses.en: and they were continually in the temple, blessing God.

title: The Gospel according to Luke
summary: The third and longest Gospel: the story of Jesus, whom Christians hold to be the deliverer sent by God, from the births of John the Baptist and Jesus to his death and resurrection, with many stories found only here, among them the Good Samaritan and the lost son. 24 chapters.

primer.a: 基督教圣经的新约开头有四卷「福音书」，各自把耶稣的事讲了一遍，《路加福音》排在第三卷，也是最长的一卷。一般认为它写在公元 80 到 90 年前后，用的是当时通行的希腊文，文笔在四卷里最讲究。书里没有写作者的名字；传统上说作者是路加，一位医生，早期传道人保罗的同伴。一般认为新约里的《使徒行传》也是他写的，是这卷书的下集。
开头四节是作者自己在说话：他告诉一位叫提阿非罗的人，自己把这些事从头仔细查考过，要按次序写下来。这是四卷福音书里唯一一处作者说「我」的地方。从第 1 章第 5 节起，就是一个不出场的人在讲故事了；引号里的话是故事里的人说的。叙述里的「他」，大多数时候指耶稣。
故事发生在大约公元 30 年前后，地点是地中海东岸的犹太人地区（今天的以色列、巴勒斯坦一带），当时归罗马帝国管；书里几次用罗马皇帝和地方官的名字来交代年代。犹太人只拜一位上帝，照着祖先摩西传下来的律法过日子，耶路撒冷有圣殿，各地有会堂。很多人在盼望上帝派一位救主来，这位救主希伯来话叫「弥赛亚」，希腊话叫「基督」。

primer.q: 读的时候会卡住的地方
primer.a: 一是前两章有两条线交替着讲：先是施洗约翰的出生，再是耶稣的出生，中间穿插三段像诗一样的颂词。二是第 3 章有一长串人名，那是耶稣的家谱，从他往上一直追到亚当；不想看可以跳过。三是从第 9 章末到第 19 章，耶稣一直「往耶路撒冷去」，路上讲了很多话和故事，地点常常不交代。四是耶稣常常打比方，这卷书里的比方故事特别多，大多数书里并不解释是什么意思；读到这样的地方，原文本来就没有说明。五是「上帝的国」：指上帝亲自作王的国度，不是指人死后去的地方。
这些词在书里反复出现，先认一下。
terms: 福音
字面是「好消息」。书里指耶稣带来的消息：上帝的国近了。
基督
希腊话，意思是「受膏的人」，就是上帝选立的那一位救主；希伯来话叫弥赛亚。后来成了耶稣的称号。
上帝的国
上帝亲自作王、他的心意行得通的国度。
人子
耶稣说到自己时最常用的称呼。字面是「人的儿子」，也是旧约里一位从上帝那里得到权柄的人物的称号。
门徒
跟着耶稣学的人。其中他特别选出十二个，又叫「使徒」。
圣灵
上帝的灵。这卷书特别常提到它：充满某个人、带着某个人行动。
法利赛人
犹太人里严守律法和各种规矩的一派，在书里常常和耶稣争论，也几次请他吃饭。
文士
专门抄写、讲解犹太律法的学者。
税吏
替罗马收税的犹太人，被同胞看不起。这卷书里他们常常和「罪人」并提。
撒玛利亚人
住在犹太和加利利之间的一族人，和犹太人世代不和。

primer.a: 全书 24 章。顺着读的话：第 1–2 章是约翰和耶稣的出生；第 3 章到第 9 章中间，是耶稣在加利利传道、治病；第 9 章末到第 19 章，是他往耶路撒冷去的路上；第 19 章末到第 24 章，是他在耶路撒冷的最后一个星期：被捕、钉十字架、复活。只想先读一段的话，读第 15 章：三个「失而复得」的故事，最后一个是离家的小儿子。

primerEn.q: What kind of book this is
primerEn.a: The New Testament of the Christian Bible opens with four "Gospels," each telling the story of Jesus; Luke is the third and the longest. It is generally dated to around 80 to 90 CE and was written in the common Greek of the time, in the most polished style of the four. The book does not name its author; by tradition he was Luke, a physician and a companion of the early preacher Paul. The Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament is generally thought to be by the same writer, as this book’s second volume.

In the first four verses the author speaks for himself: he tells a man named Theophilus that he has looked into everything carefully from the start and will write it down in order. It is the only place in the four Gospels where the author says "I." From 1:5 on, a narrator who never appears tells the story; words in quotation marks are spoken by people in it. "He" in the narration is usually Jesus.

The story takes place around 30 CE in the Jewish lands on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean (today’s Israel and Palestine), then under the Roman Empire; the book several times gives dates by naming Roman emperors and local officials. Jews worshiped one God and lived by the law handed down from their ancestor Moses, with a temple in Jerusalem and synagogues in every town. Many were waiting for God to send a deliverer, called "Messiah" in Hebrew and "Christ" in Greek.

First, the opening two chapters interleave two stories: the birth of John the Baptist, then the birth of Jesus, with three song-like speeches of praise in between. Second, chapter 3 has a long list of names: Jesus’s family line traced back to Adam; skip it if you like. Third, from the end of chapter 9 to chapter 19 Jesus is "on his way to Jerusalem," saying and telling a great deal along the road, often with no place named. Fourth, Jesus often speaks in comparisons, and this book has more story-parables than any other; most are left unexplained, and where a saying is puzzling the original usually gives no explanation either. Fifth, "the kingdom of God" means the realm in which God himself rules, not a place people go after death.
These words recur throughout the book.
terms: Good news (gospel)
In this book, the news Jesus brings: the kingdom of God has come near.
Christ
Greek for "anointed one," the deliverer chosen by God; "Messiah" in Hebrew. It later became a title for Jesus.
Kingdom of God
The realm in which God himself rules and his will is done.
Son of Man
The name Jesus most often uses for himself. Literally "son of a human being," it is also the title of a figure in the Old Testament who receives authority from God.
Disciples
Those who follow Jesus and learn from him. He singles out twelve, also called "apostles."
Holy Spirit
The Spirit of God. This book mentions it especially often: filling a person, moving a person to act.
Pharisees
A Jewish group strict about keeping the law and its many rules; in this book they often argue with Jesus, and several times invite him to dinner.
Scribes
Scholars who copied and explained the Jewish law.
Tax collectors
Jews who collected taxes for Rome and were despised by their own people. This book often pairs them with "sinners."
Samaritans
A people living between Judea and Galilee, long at odds with the Jews.

primerEn.a: The book has 24 chapters. Read straight through: chapters 1–2 are the births of John and Jesus; from chapter 3 to the middle of chapter 9 Jesus teaches and heals in Galilee; from the end of chapter 9 to chapter 19 he is on the road to Jerusalem; from the end of chapter 19 to chapter 24 comes his last week there: arrest, crucifixion, resurrection. If you want just one stretch, read chapter 15: three stories of something lost and found, the last about a younger son who leaves home.

compare: 希腊文原文用 SBL Greek New Testament（SBLGNT），只去掉了底本里的校勘符号，经文本身没有动；罗马转写是本站按通行规则机械生成的，不标重音。
白话是写给完全没接触过圣经的人看的：用平常说话的词，把谁在对谁说写清楚。原文没有、但不补就看不懂的字，一律放在圆括号（）里；括号里是通行的解释，不是经文本身。英文版贴着字面译，不加括号，两版对着看就知道哪些是补的。白话、英文和所有说明都是 AI 从希腊文译写的，没有经过圣经学者或教会审阅。
对照栏是 1919 年出版的官话和合译本（和合本），录文取自维基文库，繁体转成简体，几个异体字改成了通行写法，原书的旧式标点照录。维基文库录的是称「神」的版本；本站的白话写「上帝」。人名、地名跟和合本走，只有几处用了今天更常见的写法：约旦河、撒旦、凯撒（和合本作「约但河」「撒但」「该撒」）；和合本的「夫子」本站写「老师」，「外邦人」写「外族人」。

和合本当年依据的希腊文底本和 SBLGNT 不完全一样，所以有的地方三栏对不上，不是译错。最显眼的是第 11 章第 2–4 节：这卷书里的主祷文比《马太福音》的短，和合本这里多出几句，本站的底本没有。另有两节（17:36、23:17）底本没有、和合本印成小字注，本站留着节号，原文栏放一个「—」。和合本还有两处把相邻两节合在一起译（1:1–2、2:34–35），合译的文字放在前一节，后一节的对照栏是空的。这些地方都在那一节下面写明。
这卷书和《马可福音》《马太福音》有大量平行的段落。几卷书希腊文一样的地方，本站尽量用一样的译法；希腊文不一样的地方，译文也跟着不一样，没有互相拉齐。前两章的三段颂词原文是诗一样的句式，白话译成通顺的句子，没有硬凑成诗。
compareEn: The Greek is the SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT) with its text-critical sigla removed and nothing else changed; the romanization is generated mechanically by this site under the usual conventions, without accents.

The Chinese is written for readers who have never opened a Bible: everyday words, with who is speaking to whom made explicit. Words that are not in the Greek but are needed to follow it are put in parentheses; they give the usual explanation and are not part of the text. The English stays close to the wording and adds no parentheses, so reading the two side by side shows what was supplied. The Chinese, the English and all the notes were translated and written by AI from the Greek and have not been reviewed by biblical scholars or by any church.

The older Chinese version shown alongside is the Mandarin Union Version of 1919, taken from Chinese Wikisource, converted to simplified characters with a few variant characters normalized and its original punctuation kept. Wikisource carries the edition that calls God 神 (Shén); this site’s plain Chinese writes 上帝 (Shàngdì). Names follow the Union Version, except for a few now more commonly written another way: the Jordan, Satan and Caesar.

The Union Version was made from a Greek text that differs in places from SBLGNT, so where the columns disagree it is not always a mistranslation. The most visible case is 11:2–4: the Lord’s Prayer in this Gospel is shorter than in Matthew, and the Union Version has several extra lines here that this site’s edition lacks. Two verses (17:36; 23:17) are small-print notes in the Union Version and absent from this edition; the verse numbers are kept, with a dash in the Greek column. In two places (1:1–2; 2:34–35) the Union Version translates two verses as one; its text is shown under the first, and the second is left empty. Each such place is explained under that verse.

This Gospel has many passages parallel to Mark and Matthew. Where the Greek is the same, this site tries to translate it the same way; where the Greek differs, the translations differ too and have not been harmonized. The three songs of praise in the first two chapters are verse-like in the Greek; the Chinese renders them as plain sentences rather than forcing them into verse.
